Zhong Kui didn’t look very handsome—he had a leopard’s head, round eyes, and an iron face with curly whiskers. But he studied very hard and was very learned.
One year, Zhong Kui went to the capital for the imperial exam and did very well!
But when the emperor saw that Zhong Kui was ugly, he wouldn’t let him become an official.
Zhong Kui was so angry that he banged his head against the palace pillar and died.
When the Jade Emperor learned of this, he felt Zhong Kui was wronged. He made him the “True Lord of Demon Quelling,” responsible for catching ghosts.
Zhong Kui gained magical powers and specialized in catching evil ghosts that harmed people.
He wore a red robe and carried a sword, looking very impressive!
One day, a bad ghost came to the human world to cause trouble, scaring children so they couldn’t sleep.
Zhong Kui found out and came riding on a tiger!
“Where are you running!”
Zhong Kui waved his sword and caught the bad ghost in one stroke.
From then on, people pasted Zhong Kui’s picture on their doors, hoping he would protect their homes.
During the Dragon Boat Festival, people also hang Zhong Kui’s picture to drive away evil.
Little friends, although Zhong Kui looked scary, he was a kind and brave good god!
What the Story Teaches Us # Zhong Kui didn’t look good on the outside, but he was kind and protected everyone from bad ghosts. This story teaches us not to judge by appearances—what matters is having a kind heart.
title: 022 Zhong Kui Catches Ghosts

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, there was a kind girl named Meng Jiangnu.
She married a scholar named Fan Xiliang, and they loved each other very much.
But the Emperor Qinshihuang was building the Great Wall and took Fan Xiliang away as a laborer.
Meng Jiangnu missed her husband very much. She decided to go to the Great Wall to find him.
She walked and walked for a long, long time, finally reaching the Great Wall.
“Where is my husband Fan Xiliang?” Meng Jiangnu asked.
But someone told her: “Fan Xiliang has already died from exhaustion. He’s buried under the Great Wall.”
Meng Jiangnu was heartbroken and cried loudly.
“Waaah… waaah…”
She cried and cried, crying until the sky grew dark.
Suddenly—
“Rumble!”
Eight hundred miles of the Great Wall collapsed from her tears!
Meng Jiangnu finally found her husband’s bones. She held them, heartbroken.
Later, Meng Jiangnu buried her husband properly and jumped into the sea to be with him.
Little friends, the Great Wall was built with many people’s lives. We should cherish our happy lives today.
What the Story Teaches Us # Meng Jiangnu’s love for her husband was very deep. This story teaches us to cherish time with our families, and to remember that behind many great buildings are the sacrifices of ordinary people.
title: 023 Meng Jiangnu Weeps at the Great Wall

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, there was a girl named Zhu Yingtai who really wanted to study.
But in those days, girls couldn’t go to school.
Zhu Yingtai thought of a way: she dressed as a boy, pretending to be a young man, and went to school.
At school, Zhu Yingtai met a classmate named Liang Shanbo.
They studied together, played together, and became best friends.
Three years later, Zhu Yingtai had to go home. Liang Shanbo walked with her for eighteen miles.
Zhu Yingtai said: “Brother Liang, I have a younger sister who looks exactly like me. Would you like to marry her?”
Liang Shanbo happily agreed.
Later, when Liang Shanbo went to Zhu Yingtai’s house to propose, he discovered the “younger sister” was Zhu Yingtai herself!
Liang Shanbo was overjoyed. But Zhu Yingtai’s father had already promised her to someone else.
Liang Shanbo was so heartbroken he fell ill and died.
On Zhu Yingtai’s wedding day, her bridal sedan chair passed by Liang Shanbo’s grave.
Zhu Yingtai jumped out of the sedan chair and cried loudly at the grave.
Suddenly—
“Rumble!”
The grave cracked open, and Zhu Yingtai jumped inside.
The grave closed again.
After a while, two beautiful butterflies flew out of the grave.
They danced among the flowers, together forever.
Little friends, this is the story of “transforming into butterflies.” Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai finally got to be together.
What the Story Teaches Us # Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai’s friendship turned into love. They would rather become butterflies than be apart. This story teaches us that true feelings are precious, and we should bravely pursue our own happiness.
title: 024 The Butterfly Lovers

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, the Jade Emperor wanted to choose twelve animals as zodiac signs.
He announced: “Tomorrow morning, whoever arrives at the Heavenly Court first will be number one!”
The Rat and the Cat were good friends. They agreed to go together.
The Rat said: “Brother Cat, I can’t wake up. You wake me up.”
The Cat said: “Okay, I’ll definitely wake you up.”
The next day, the Cat overslept. The Rat went alone.
When the Rat reached the river, the water was too wide to cross.
Just then, the Ox came along.
The Rat said: “Uncle Ox, please carry me across the river!”
The Ox agreed. The Rat sat on the Ox’s back and crossed the river.
When they were almost at the Heavenly Court, the Rat jumped off the Ox’s back and rushed in first!
“I’m number one!” the Rat cheered happily.
The Ox was second, the Tiger third, the Rabbit fourth…
The Dragon flew in, fifth; The Snake slithered in, sixth; The Horse ran in, seventh; The Sheep walked in, eighth; The Monkey hopped in, ninth; The Chicken flapped in, tenth; The Dog ran in, eleventh; The Pig waddled in, twelfth.
The Cat woke up and ran as fast as he could, but only came in thirteenth. He wasn’t chosen.
From then on, the Cat chases the Rat whenever he sees it, because the Rat didn’t wake him up!
Little friends, what’s your zodiac animal?
What the Story Teaches Us # The story of the twelve zodiac animals teaches us to keep our promises. The Rat didn’t wake the Cat, so cats and rats became enemies.
title: 025 The Twelve Zodiac Animals

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in ancient Greece, humans didn’t have fire.
People could only eat raw food. At night, everything was dark. In winter, they shivered from the cold.
There was a god named Prometheus who felt sorry for humans.
Prometheus thought: “I must help humans get fire!”
He quietly went to Mount Olympus. While the sun god Apollo wasn’t looking, he stole a spark from the sun chariot.
Prometheus hid the fire spark in a reed tube and brought it to humans.
“Look! This is fire!” Prometheus said.
People used fire to roast meat, keep warm, and light up the night. Life became much better!
But when Zeus, the king of gods, found out, he was very angry.
“How dare you steal fire!” Zeus chained Prometheus to a high mountain.
Every day, a giant eagle came to peck at Prometheus’s liver.
Prometheus was in great pain, but he didn’t regret it because he had helped humans.
Later, the hero Hercules passed by, shot the eagle, and saved Prometheus.
Little friends, Prometheus was willing to suffer to help humans. He was truly a kind god!
What the Story Teaches Us # Prometheus was willing to suffer to help humans. He teaches us that helping others is worthwhile, even if it comes at a cost.
title: 026 Prometheus Brings Fire

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, Zeus wanted to punish humans. He created a woman named Pandora.
Zeus gave Pandora a beautiful box and said: “You must never open this box!”
Pandora was very curious: “What could be inside the box?”
She looked at the box every day, feeling itchy with curiosity.
“Just one peek, it should be okay, right?” Pandora thought.
Finally one day, Pandora couldn’t resist anymore. She opened the box—
“Whoosh!”
Many terrible things flew out of the box: sickness, pain, jealousy, greed, anger…
These bad things flew all over the world. People started getting sick, arguing, and feeling sad.
Pandora was scared and quickly closed the box.
“Oh no! I’ve caused trouble!” Pandora cried.
Just then, a tiny voice came from inside the box: “Don’t cry, I’m still in here!”
Pandora opened the box again, and a glowing little fairy flew out.
It was “Hope”!
From then on, although there were bad things in the world, people always had hope in their hearts.
Little friends, no matter what difficulties you face, remember: hope is always there!
What the Story Teaches Us # Pandora opened the box and released bad things, but she also released hope. This story teaches us that no matter what difficulties we face, we should keep hope alive, because hope is always in our hearts.
title: 027 Pandora's Box

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a handsome sun god named Apollo.
Apollo was the son of Zeus. He was very handsome, with golden hair that shone brightly.
Every morning, Apollo drove his golden sun chariot, rising from the east.
“Rumble!”
The sun chariot crossed the sky, bringing light and warmth to the earth.
Apollo had many talents: he could play the lyre beautifully, his music was enchanting; he was an excellent archer, his aim always true; he could also see the future and knew what would happen.
One day, a giant serpent was causing trouble in a valley, hurting many small animals.
Apollo found out, picked up his bow and arrows, and found the serpent.
“Whoosh!”
Apollo shot the serpent with one arrow, protecting the animals in the valley.
Everyone thanked Apollo and called him the “God of Light.”
Apollo also taught people to play instruments, sing, and heal the sick. He was one of the most loved gods.
Little friends, the sun rises every day, just like Apollo driving his sun chariot, bringing us light!
What the Story Teaches Us # Apollo used his powers to help everyone and protect the weak. He teaches us to use our abilities to help others and make the world more beautiful.
title: 028 Apollo the Sun God

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a beautiful moon goddess named Artemis.
Artemis was Apollo’s twin sister. She was very beautiful, with silver hair that shone like moonlight.
She was the goddess of hunting, often carrying a silver bow and arrows, running through the forests.
Artemis especially loved small animals. She protected the deer, rabbits, and various creatures in the forest.
One day, a hunter sneaked into the forest, trying to catch a little deer.
“Don’t hurt it!” Artemis appeared.
She raised her bow and arrow. The hunter dropped his weapon in fear and ran away.
The little deer looked at Artemis gratefully and rubbed against her leg.
Artemis patted the little deer’s head: “Don’t worry, I’ll protect you.”
At night, Artemis drove her silver moon chariot, patrolling the night sky.
She was always followed by a group of nymphs. Together they danced and sang under the moonlight.
Little friends, when you see the moon at night, that’s Artemis watching over us!
What the Story Teaches Us # Artemis protected the small animals in the forest. She teaches us to love animals, protect nature, and give small animals a safe home.
title: 029 Artemis the Moon Goddess

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a goddess of wisdom named Athena.
Athena was born from Zeus’s head. When she was born, she was already wearing armor and holding a spear, looking very impressive.
Athena was very clever. She taught people many skills: farming, weaving, making pottery…
There was a city where people wanted to invite a god to protect them.
Both Athena and the sea god Poseidon wanted to go.
Poseidon struck the ground with his trident and created a warhorse.
Athena touched the ground with her spear and created an olive tree.
“The warhorse can be used for battle, but the olive tree bears fruit to eat, and oil can be pressed from it,” Athena said.
The people thought the olive tree was more useful, so they chose Athena.
This city was called “Athens,” and it became the most famous city in Greece.
Athena also protected the hero Odysseus, helping him overcome many difficulties.
Little friends, Athena teaches us: wisdom is more important than strength!
What the Story Teaches Us # Athena used wisdom to help people, not force. This story teaches us to use our brains when facing problems—wisdom can solve problems better than strength.
title: 030 Athena's Wisdom

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a mighty hero named Hercules.
Hercules was the son of Zeus. He was incredibly strong and famous from childhood.
One day, Hercules made a mistake and had to complete twelve difficult tasks to atone.
First task: Defeat a lion with impenetrable skin. Hercules strangled the lion with his bare hands!
Second task: Defeat the nine-headed serpent. Every time Hercules cut off one head, two more grew. He figured out a way to burn the wounds with fire, finally defeating the serpent!
Third task: Capture the golden-horned deer. This deer ran very fast. Hercules chased it for a year and finally caught it.
Fourth task: Capture the wild boar…
Hercules completed task after task, finishing all twelve!
He defeated various monsters, cleaned dirty stables, and even brought back a three-headed dog from the underworld.
Hercules became the greatest hero in Greece!
Little friends, Hercules wasn’t afraid of difficulties and bravely completed all his tasks.
What the Story Teaches Us # Hercules never backed down from difficulties. He teaches us to face problems bravely, solve them one by one, and we will surely succeed.
title: 031 Hercules' Twelve Labors

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a hero named Perseus.
One day, a king gave Perseus a difficult challenge: “Go defeat Medusa!”
Medusa was a terrible monster. Her hair was made of snakes, and anyone who looked into her eyes would turn to stone!
Perseus was scared, but he agreed.
The goddess Athena came to help him. She gave him a shield as shiny as a mirror.
“Don’t look directly at Medusa’s eyes. Look at her reflection in the shield!” Athena said.
Perseus went to the cave where Medusa lived.
He held up the shield, looking at Medusa’s reflection, and slowly approached her.
Medusa was sleeping, her snake hair hissing “Sss… sss…”
Perseus raised his sword and struck—
Medusa was defeated!
Perseus put Medusa’s head in a bag and returned home victoriously.
Later, Perseus used Medusa’s head to help many people in need.
Little friends, Perseus used wisdom and courage to complete his task!
What the Story Teaches Us # Perseus didn’t just use brute force—he used wisdom to find the way to defeat Medusa. This story teaches us to use our brains when facing powerful difficulties and find the right method.
title: 032 Perseus and Medusa

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a hero named Theseus.
On the island of Crete, there was a terrible maze. Inside lived a monster called the Minotaur.
The Minotaur had a bull’s head and a human body. It was very fierce.
Every year, Athens had to send seven boys and seven girls to be eaten by the Minotaur.
Theseus decided to defeat the Minotaur and save everyone.
He went to Crete, where the princess Ariadne fell in love with him.
“The maze is very complex. Once you go in, you can’t get out,” the princess said. “I’ll give you a ball of thread. Unwind it as you walk, and you’ll find your way back.”
Theseus took the thread and entered the maze.
He unwound the thread as he walked, leaving a long trail on the ground.
Finally, Theseus found the Minotaur!
After a fierce battle, Theseus defeated the Minotaur.
Then, following the thread, he led everyone out of the maze.
Theseus became a hero of Athens!
Little friends, Theseus used the princess’s thread to successfully find his way out of the maze. This is the story of “Ariadne’s thread”!
What the Story Teaches Us # Theseus bravely faced the monster and cleverly used the thread. This story teaches us that bravery and wisdom are both important, and sometimes we need help from others to succeed.
title: 033 Theseus and the Minotaur

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a boy named Icarus.
He and his father Daedalus were locked in a high tower with no way out.
Daedalus was a very clever craftsman. He thought of a way to escape.
He used bird feathers and wax to make two pairs of wings.
“Icarus, let’s fly out!” Daedalus said.
Before leaving, his father warned Icarus: “Remember, don’t fly too low—the sea spray will wet your wings. Don’t fly too high either—the sun’s heat will melt the wax. Fly in the middle!”
“I understand, Father!” Icarus said.
They flapped their wings and flew into the sky!
“Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!”
Icarus thought flying was so much fun! He flew higher and higher…
“Icarus, you’re too high! Come down!” his father shouted.
But Icarus was having too much fun. He forgot his father’s words.
The sun got closer and hotter…
“Snap!”
The wax on his wings melted, and the feathers scattered!
Icarus fell from the sky and dropped into the sea.
Little friends, Icarus got into danger because he didn’t listen to his father. We must remember: listening to mom and dad is important!
What the Story Teaches Us # Icarus flew too high because he didn’t listen to his father’s warning and got into danger. This story teaches us to listen to our parents and not forget safety just because we’re having too much fun.
title: 034 Icarus' Wings

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a musician named Orpheus.
Orpheus played the lyre so beautifully that even stones and trees were moved by his music.
He had a beautiful wife named Eurydice, and they loved each other very much.
One day, Eurydice was accidentally bitten by a snake and died.
Orpheus was heartbroken. He decided to go to the underworld to bring his wife back.
He played his lyre and entered the underworld.
The king and queen of the underworld were moved by his music and agreed to let Eurydice go with him.
But there was one condition: “Before you walk out of the underworld, you must not look back at your wife.”
“I promise!” Orpheus said.
Orpheus led his wife back, holding back from looking the whole way.
Almost at the exit, Orpheus missed his wife so much that he couldn’t help looking back—
“No!” Eurydice was pulled back into the underworld.
Orpheus was so sad. He played sorrowful music and wandered in the forests.
Little friends, Orpheus couldn’t hold back from looking because he missed his wife too much. This story teaches us: sometimes we must control our feelings to achieve our goals.
What the Story Teaches Us # Orpheus lost his wife because he couldn’t hold back from looking. This story teaches us to keep our promises, and sometimes we need to control our feelings and persist to the end.
title: 035 Orpheus and Eurydice

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a shiny golden apple.
Once, the gods held a banquet but didn’t invite Eris, the goddess of discord.
Eris was angry. She secretly threw a golden apple at the banquet.
The golden apple had written on it: “For the fairest goddess!”
Three goddesses wanted this golden apple: Hera, Athena, and Aphrodite.
They argued and argued, none willing to give in.
Finally, they decided to let a mortal judge.
This mortal was named Paris, a handsome shepherd.
Hera said: “Choose me, and I’ll make you a king!” Athena said: “Choose me, and I’ll make you the wisest!” Aphrodite said: “Choose me, and I’ll let you marry the most beautiful woman in the world!”
Paris thought about it and gave the golden apple to Aphrodite.
Hera and Athena were angry. They swore to take revenge on Paris.
Later, Paris married the most beautiful woman in the world, Helen. But Helen was already someone else’s wife.
This started a great war—the Trojan War.
Little friends, a tiny golden apple caused such big trouble!
What the Story Teaches Us # The golden apple story teaches us that sometimes small arguments can cause big troubles. We should learn to share and not fight over things.
title: 036 The Golden Apple

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, the Greeks and Trojans fought for ten whole years!
The city of Troy was so strong that the Greeks couldn’t break through.
The clever Odysseus thought of a plan.
“Let’s build a big wooden horse, hide soldiers inside, and pretend to retreat!” Odysseus said.
The Greeks built a super big wooden horse and hid soldiers inside.
Then, the Greek army pretended to retreat, leaving only the big wooden horse.
The Trojans thought the Greeks had run away and were overjoyed!
“This big wooden horse is a gift the Greeks left behind. Let’s bring it into the city!” the Trojans said.
At night, the Trojans celebrated their victory and drank lots of wine. Everyone fell asleep.
In the middle of the night, the Greek soldiers hidden in the wooden horse quietly climbed out.
They opened the city gates, and the Greek army outside rushed in!
“Charge!”
The Trojans were still sleeping when they were defeated.
The Greeks won with wisdom!
Little friends, this is the story of the “Trojan Horse.” It teaches us that sometimes wisdom is more powerful than force!
What the Story Teaches Us # The Greeks used wisdom to defeat a powerful enemy. This story teaches us to use our brains when facing difficulties—wisdom can defeat strength.
title: 037 The Trojan Horse

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, after the Trojan War ended, Odysseus began his journey home.
But his journey was filled with dangers.
He met a Cyclops! The giant locked him and his companions in a cave, wanting to eat them.
Odysseus thought of a plan. He used a sharp wooden stick to blind the giant and escaped with his companions.
He then met the witch Circe, who turned Odysseus’s companions into pigs!
Odysseus saved his companions and continued forward.
He also encountered the Sirens. Their singing was so beautiful that anyone who heard it would jump into the sea.
Odysseus had his companions seal their ears with wax and tied himself to the mast, passing safely through.
He also passed through the strait where monsters Scylla and Charybdis lived, losing many companions.
Finally, after ten years, Odysseus returned home!
His wife Penelope had been waiting for him all this time. They were finally reunited.
Little friends, Odysseus went through many hardships but never gave up. He was truly a brave and clever man!
What the Story Teaches Us # Odysseus faced many difficulties but never gave up. This story teaches us that no matter how hard the journey home, we must persist. Our families are waiting for us, and we should cherish them.
title: 038 Odysseus' Journey Home

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a girl who ran very fast, named Atalanta.
Atalanta loved running from childhood. She could run faster than boys!
Many boys wanted to marry her, but Atalanta didn’t want to get married.
She said: “Anyone who wants to marry me must race me. Win, and I’ll marry you. Lose, and you’ll be punished.”
Many young men came to challenge, but all lost to Atalanta.
There was a young man named Hippomenes who really liked Atalanta.
He asked the goddess Aphrodite for help.
The goddess gave him three golden apples.
The race began!
“Ready—go!”
Atalanta ran very fast, with Hippomenes chasing behind.
Just as Atalanta was about to win, Hippomenes threw out a golden apple.
The golden apple shone brightly. Atalanta couldn’t resist stopping to pick it up.
Hippomenes took the chance to pass her!
Atalanta caught up again, and Hippomenes threw out the second golden apple.
Atalanta stopped again to pick it up…
Like this, Hippomenes won the race!
Although Atalanta lost, she thought Hippomenes was very clever, so she married him.
Little friends, Hippomenes used wisdom to win the race!
What the Story Teaches Us # Hippomenes used golden apples to win the race. This story teaches us that sometimes wisdom is more important than speed—we should use our brains to find solutions.
title: 039 Atalanta's Race

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a boy named Phaethon.
His father was the sun god Apollo.
One day, Phaethon said to his father: “Father, I want to drive your sun chariot!”
Apollo was worried: “The sun chariot is too hard to control. You’ll get hurt.”
But Phaethon insisted on trying.
Apollo had no choice but to agree.
The next morning, Phaethon climbed onto the sun chariot.
“Let’s go!” he shouted.
The sun chariot flew into the sky!
But the horses were too strong. Phaethon couldn’t control them.
The sun chariot flew too high sometimes, freezing the sky; other times it flew too low, burning the earth.
“Help!” Phaethon was terrified.
Zeus saw this and worried the sun chariot would destroy the world.
He threw a lightning bolt—
“Boom!”
The sun chariot was hit, and Phaethon fell from the sky.
Apollo was heartbroken. He regretted letting his son drive the sun chariot.
Little friends, Phaethon got into danger because he didn’t listen to his father. We must remember: some things we can’t do yet—we should listen to adults!
What the Story Teaches Us # Phaethon got into danger driving the sun chariot because he didn’t listen to his father’s advice. This story teaches us to listen to our parents—some things are too dangerous for us to do when we’re too young.
title: 040 Phaethon Drives the Sun Chariot

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a boy named Narcissus.
Narcissus was very handsome. Many girls liked him.
There was a nymph named Echo who also liked Narcissus.
But Narcissus was too proud. He didn’t like anyone.
Echo was heartbroken. She hid in a cave and stopped speaking. She could only repeat the last words others said.
One day, Narcissus came to the river to drink water.
He saw a beautiful reflection in the water—his own reflection.
“Wow, this person is so beautiful!” Narcissus fell in love with his own reflection.
He talked to the water every day, wanting to catch the person in the water.
“Hello!” “Hello!” Echo replied from the cave. “I love you!” “I love you!” Echo replied.
But Narcissus ignored Echo. He only loved his own reflection.
Finally, Narcissus became so sad that he turned into a flower by the river.
This flower is called the “daffodil.”
Little friends, Narcissus loved his own appearance too much and turned into a flower. This story teaches us not to love only ourselves—we should learn to love others.
What the Story Teaches Us # Narcissus only loved himself and finally turned into a daffodil. This story teaches us not to be too proud, not to love only ourselves, and to learn to care for and love the people around us.
title: 041 Narcissus and Echo

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a girl named Psyche.
She was so beautiful that people said she was more beautiful than the goddess Aphrodite.
Aphrodite was jealous. She asked her son Cupid to punish Psyche.
Cupid was the god of love. He had wings and a golden arrow. Anyone struck by his golden arrow would fall in love.
But when Cupid saw Psyche, he fell in love with her himself!
Cupid brought Psyche to a beautiful palace. But he only came at night and wouldn’t let her see what he looked like.
Psyche really wanted to know what her husband looked like.
One night, she secretly lit a lamp and saw Cupid.
“So you’re a god!” Psyche cried out.
Cupid woke up. He was angry that Psyche didn’t trust him and flew away.
Psyche regretted it. She searched everywhere for Cupid, going through many hardships.
Finally, Zeus was moved by her sincerity and made her a goddess.
Psyche and Cupid were finally together, living happily on Mount Olympus.
Little friends, the love story of Psyche and Cupid teaches us: trust and sincerity are very important!
What the Story Teaches Us # Psyche almost lost Cupid because she didn’t trust him. This story teaches us that in love and friendship, trust is very important—we should believe in the people around us.
title: 042 Cupid and Psyche

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a god who could fly very fast, named Hermes.
Hermes was the son of Zeus. He looked very cute, with little wings on his feet.
With these wings, Hermes could fly very, very fast!
He was the messenger of the gods, responsible for delivering messages.
On the day Hermes was born, he did something mischievous.
He sneaked out and saw Apollo’s cattle.
“These cattle look nice. Let me take a few to play with!” Hermes thought.
He drove away fifty cattle. He also tied their feet together so they walked backward, making it impossible to find their footprints!
Apollo discovered his cattle were missing and searched everywhere.
Finally, he found Hermes.
“You stole my cattle!” Apollo said angrily.
Hermes had to admit it. He even gave Apollo a lyre he had made as an apology.
Apollo heard the lyre’s sound and thought it was beautiful, so he forgave Hermes.
From then on, Hermes became the protector of music and travel.
Little friends, although Hermes was mischievous, he was very clever and talented!
What the Story Teaches Us # Hermes was mischievous, but he admitted his mistakes and used his talents to make up for them. This story teaches us to admit when we do wrong and make amends with our actions.
title: 043 The Story of Hermes

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a god of the sea named Poseidon.
Poseidon was Zeus’s brother. He lived in a palace deep under the sea.
He had a trident. Just one wave, and the sea would churn with waves!
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
Poseidon had many seahorses that pulled his chariot, speeding through the sea.
One day, Poseidon wanted to create a new animal.
He thought about it and combined a horse’s body with a fish tail.
Like this, the seahorse was born!
Seahorses look very interesting: a head like a horse, a curled tail like a monkey, and a hard shell on their body.
The most amazing thing is that seahorse daddies give birth to babies!
The seahorse mommy puts eggs in the seahorse daddy’s tummy, and the seahorse daddy hatches the baby seahorses.
Poseidon also created dolphins, octopuses, starfish, and other sea creatures.
He protected fishermen, keeping them safe at sea.
But Poseidon had a bad temper sometimes. When he got angry, storms would rise on the sea.
Little friends, when you see waves churning, that’s Poseidon waving his trident!
What the Story Teaches Us # Poseidon created various sea creatures. This story teaches us that there are many amazing animals in the sea, and we should protect the ocean so they have a beautiful home.
title: 044 Poseidon and the Seahorse

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Greek mythology, there was a beautiful goddess of spring named Persephone.
She was the daughter of Demeter, the goddess of the earth. Persephone was very beautiful.
One day, Persephone was picking flowers in a meadow.
“Wow, this flower is so pretty!” She picked a narcissus.
Suddenly, the earth cracked open!
Hades, the god of the underworld, drove his black chariot up from underground.
He grabbed Persephone and took her to the underworld!
When Demeter found her daughter missing, she was heartbroken.
She was so sad that she forgot to take care of the earth.
Flowers withered, leaves fell, and the earth became desolate.
People had no food to eat and were very hungry.
Zeus found out and ordered Hades to return Persephone.
But Persephone had eaten six pomegranate seeds in the underworld.
If you eat food from the underworld, you can’t leave completely.
Finally, they made an agreement:
Persephone would stay in the underworld for six months each year, and on earth for six months.
When she’s on earth, Demeter is happy, and it’s spring and summer; When she’s in the underworld, Demeter is sad, and it’s autumn and winter.
Little friends, this is why we have four seasons!
What the Story Teaches Us # Persephone’s story explains the changing of seasons. This story teaches us that nature has its own patterns, and spring will always bring warmth and hope.
title: 045 Hades and Persephone

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in the far north, there was a father of all gods named Odin.
Odin was the most powerful god in Norse mythology. He had only one eye and rode an eight-legged horse.
He was very wise and knew many things.
One day, Odin heard about a Well of Wisdom. Drinking from it would make someone super wise.
The guardian of this well was Mimir, a very wise giant.
Odin came to the Well of Wisdom and said: “I want to drink from the well.”
Mimir said: “You can, but you must pay a price.”
“What price?” Odin asked.
“One of your eyes,” Mimir said.
Odin thought about it. To gain wisdom, he was willing to pay this price.
He took out one of his eyes and threw it into the well.
Then, he drank from the well.
“Gulp! Gulp!”
Suddenly, Odin knew all the secrets of the world! He knew what had happened in the past and what would happen in the future.
From then on, Odin became the wisest god.
Little friends, Odin paid a great price to gain wisdom. This story teaches us: knowledge is precious, and we should study hard!
What the Story Teaches Us # Odin was willing to sacrifice one of his eyes to gain wisdom. This story teaches us that knowledge is very precious and worth our hard work to pursue.
title: 046 Odin and the Well of Wisdom

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a mighty god of thunder named Thor.
Thor was Odin’s son. He was very strong, with a red beard and incredible power!
He had a magical hammer called “Mjölnir.”
This hammer was amazing! When thrown, it could defeat any enemy, and it would automatically fly back to Thor’s hand.
“Boom!”
When Thor swung his hammer, thunder would crash in the sky. That’s why he’s the god of thunder!
One day, a giant king stole Thor’s hammer.
“If you want the hammer back, marry the goddess Freya to me!” the giant king said.
Thor was desperate. Without his hammer, he couldn’t protect the realm of the gods.
The trickster god Loki thought of a plan: “Thor, dress up as a bride, and I’ll help you get the hammer back!”
Thor put on a bride’s dress, pretending to be Freya, and went to the giant’s palace.
The giant king was happy and put the hammer on the “bride’s” lap.
Thor grabbed the hammer and jumped up!
“Boom!”
He used the hammer to defeat the giant king and got his hammer back.
Little friends, Thor used wisdom to get his hammer back and protect the realm of the gods!
What the Story Teaches Us # Thor was very strong, but sometimes he needed to use his brain too. This story teaches us that strength and wisdom are both important, and we should learn to use them flexibly.
title: 047 Thor's Hammer

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a god who loved playing tricks, named Loki.
Loki was very clever but also very mischievous. He often played pranks on other gods, making them angry but also amused.
Once, Loki secretly cut off the goddess Sif’s beautiful golden hair.
When Sif woke up and found herself bald, she cried heartbrokenly.
Her husband Thor was furious and wanted to beat Loki.
“Don’t be angry, I’ll make it up to her!” Loki said.
Loki found dwarf craftsmen and had them make a golden wig.
This golden wig was magical—as soon as it was put on, it became real hair!
Sif had beautiful golden hair again, even more beautiful than before.
Loki also had the dwarves make many treasures: Thor’s hammer, Odin’s ring, Frey’s ship…
All these treasures were given to the gods.
Although Loki loved playing pranks, sometimes he could be helpful.
But Loki’s pranks became more and more excessive, and finally, he became an enemy of the gods.
Little friends, Loki’s story teaches us: pranks should be moderate. Going too far will make you lose friends.
What the Story Teaches Us # Loki was clever, but his pranks went too far, and he finally lost his friends. This story teaches us to be moderate when joking and not hurt others.
title: 048 Loki's Mischief

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a super big tree called Yggdrasil.
This tree was so big that its roots connected three worlds:
The upper roots connected to the world of the gods, where Odin and other gods lived; The middle roots connected to the world of humans, where we live; The lower roots connected to the world of giants and the underworld.
The trunk of the World Tree held up the entire universe!
Many magical animals lived in the tree:
A clever little squirrel ran up and down, delivering messages; A great eagle stood at the top, watching everything; A snake coiled around the roots, gnawing on the bark; Four little deer jumped among the branches.
Every day, goddesses came to water the World Tree, making it grow tall and strong.
The World Tree would never die. It protected all the worlds.
The Norse people believed that this tree was the center of the universe, and all life was connected to it.
Little friends, the World Tree is like our nature. We should take good care of it!
What the Story Teaches Us # The World Tree connects all worlds and protects all life. This story teaches us that nature is the home of all life, and we should love trees and protect the environment.
title: 049 Yggdrasil the World Tree

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a group of brave warrior women called the Valkyries.
They were Odin’s maidens. They wore shiny armor and rode white horses, flying over battlefields.
“Whoosh! Whoosh! Whoosh!”
The Valkyries flew through the sky. Their armor sparkled—this is the Northern Lights!
The Valkyries’ job was to find the bravest warriors on battlefields and bring them to Valhalla palace.
Valhalla was Odin’s palace, where there was endless meat to eat and endless mead to drink.
The brave warriors trained there, preparing for the final battle.
The Valkyries had many names: Brynhild, Göndul, Rota…
They were all very beautiful but also very powerful!
Once, the Valkyrie Brynhild fell in love with a mortal hero.
Odin was angry and trapped her in a mountain of fire.
Later, the hero Sigurd passed through the flames and saved Brynhild.
Little friends, the Valkyries were both brave and beautiful. They watched over brave people!
What the Story Teaches Us # The Valkyries were brave and strong. They chose brave people. This story teaches us to be brave—brave people earn respect and honor.
title: 050 The Valkyries

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a god named Balder. He was the god of light, the most beautiful and kind god.
Balder had a dream: “I will die!”
The gods were worried and asked Frigg, the goddess of love, to protect Balder.
Frigg went to everything in the world and said: “Don’t hurt Balder!”
Everything promised: “I won’t hurt Balder!”
But Frigg forgot one thing—the mistletoe plant.
One day, the gods were playing a game. They threw things at Balder to see if he would get hurt.
“Whoosh! Bang! Splash!”
Everything missed Balder. He was safe!
But Loki, the trickster god, found out about the mistletoe.
Loki made an arrow from mistletoe wood and gave it to Balder’s blind brother, Hodr.
“Throw this at Balder,” Loki said.
Hodr threw the arrow—
“Whoosh!”
The arrow hit Balder! Balder fell to the ground and died.
All the gods were heartbroken. They tried everything to bring Balder back, but nothing worked.
The gods were very angry at Loki and punished him severely.
Little friends, Balder’s story teaches us: even the most powerful things can be hurt if we’re not careful.
What the Story Teaches Us # Balder was hurt because of a small mistake. This story teaches us to be careful and protect the things we love.
title: 051 Balder the God of Light

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a prophecy about the end of the gods.
It was called Ragnarok—the end of the gods.
The prophecy said: great battles would come, the sky would darken, and the world would end.
But Ragnarok was not really the end. After the darkness, a new world would be born.
The gods knew about Ragnarok and prepared for it.
Odin, the father of the gods, rode his horse Sleipnir.
Thor, the thunder god, held his hammer Mjölnir.
All the gods gathered to fight the bad forces.
“Whoosh! Boom! Crash!”
The sky turned red. Mountains crumbled. The ocean rose.
The great wolf Fenrir broke free from his chains and swallowed the sun.
The sea serpent Jörmungandr rose from the ocean and fought Thor.
Thor fought the sea serpent and killed it, but he was poisoned by its venom.
Thor fell to the ground, and the sea serpent also died.
After the great battle, a new world was born.
A new sun and moon appeared. A new earth grew.
The gods who survived would live in the new world.
Little friends, Ragnarok teaches us: even in darkness, hope remains. After every end, a new beginning comes.
What the Story Teaches Us # Ragnarok describes the end and rebirth of the world. This story teaches us: no matter how dark things get, there is always hope for a better tomorrow.
title: 052 Ragnarok

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a goddess of love and beauty named Freya.
She was very beautiful and wore a beautiful golden necklace called Brísingamen.
The necklace sparkled like the stars in the sky.
One day, the god Loki saw the necklace and wanted it.
Loki went to Freya and said: “Give me the golden necklace!”
Freya said: “No! It’s my precious possession!”
Loki was angry. He decided to steal it.
Loki turned himself into a fly and flew into Freya’s room.
Freya was sleeping. Loki flew down and took the golden necklace.
“Whoosh!”
Loki flew away with the necklace.
Freya woke up and found her necklace was gone!
She was heartbroken. She went to Odin, the father of the gods.
“Someone stole my golden necklace!” Freya cried.
Odin asked: “Who stole it?”
Freya said: “I don’t know.”
Odin sent his servants to find the thief.
Finally, they found Loki. Loki had to return the golden necklace to Freya.
Freya was happy to get her necklace back.
Little friends, stealing is not good. We should respect other people’s belongings.
What the Story Teaches Us # Loki stole Freya’s necklace and had to return it. This story teaches us: stealing is wrong, and we must respect other people’s property.
title: 053 Freya and the Golden Necklace

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there was a god named Heimdall.
He was the guardian of the rainbow bridge called Bifrost.
The rainbow bridge connected the earth to Asgard, the home of the gods.
Heimdall stood on the rainbow bridge and watched for enemies.
He had very good eyesight—he could see things from very far away.
He could also hear things from very far away.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
He could hear a leaf falling from a tree a mile away!
One day, Heimdall saw something coming toward the rainbow bridge.
“Who is there?” he shouted.
It was Loki, the trickster god, trying to sneak into Asgard.
Heimdall blocked the way: “You can’t pass! You’re not allowed!”
Loki tried to trick him, but Heimdall was too smart.
Heimdall also had a special horn called Gjallarhorn.
When enemies approached, he would blow the horn:
“Beep! Beep! Beep!”
All the gods would hear the horn and come to defend Asgard.
Little friends, Heimdall was a brave and responsible guardian. He watched over everyone to keep them safe.
What the Story Teaches Us # Heimdall was a responsible guardian who protected Asgard. This story teaches us to be responsible and protect the people we care about.
title: 054 Heimdall Guards the Rainbow Bridge

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Norse mythology, there were magical creatures called elves.
There were light elves and dark elves.
The light elves lived in beautiful places. They shone like stars.
They liked to sing and dance. They helped humans sometimes.
The dark elves lived underground. They were small and wore dark clothes.
They were good at making things.
They made Thor’s hammer, Odin’s ring, and Freya’s golden necklace.
They were called dwarves!
Dwarves were small but very skilled.
They could dig beautiful gems from the ground.
They made beautiful jewelry and weapons.
Once, Loki and a dwarf made a bet.
Who could make the best thing?
The dwarves made many wonderful things.
Loki lost the bet. His mouth was sewn shut!
Besides elves and dwarves, there were forest spirits.
They liked to play tricks on people.
Sometimes they helped people too.
If you got lost in the forest, the forest spirits might be playing with you!
Little friends, Norse mythology has many magical creatures. They make the world more interesting!
What the Story Teaches Us # The elves and dwarves were magical creatures with different talents. This story teaches us that everyone has their own special abilities.
title: 055 Forest Elves and Dwarves

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a powerful sun god named Ra.
Ra was very old and very wise. He was the king of all gods.
One day, Ra decided to create the world.
He took some of his own body parts and made everything:
His eye became the sun, shining in the sky. His tears became the moon. His breath became the wind. His blood became the rivers.
Ra created humans from his sweat and tears.
“Live well, humans!” Ra said. “Take care of each other.”
But humans forgot Ra’s words and started doing bad things.
Ra was sad and angry. He decided to punish humans.
He sent his daughter, Hathor, to destroy them.
But the gods stopped Hathor. They made a compromise:
Ra would live on earth for a while, then go back to the sky.
Ra agreed. He lived on earth for a long time, watching over humans.
Ra taught humans to build temples and worship the gods.
Little friends, Ra created the world and taught humans how to live well.
What the Story Teaches Us # Ra created the world and taught humans to be good. This story teaches us to be grateful and take care of our world.
title: 056 Ra Creates the World

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a god named Osiris.
He was the god of the dead and the ruler of the underworld.
Osiris was a good king who taught people to be kind and just.
He married his sister, the goddess Isis.
Isis was very wise and powerful. She loved Osiris very much.
But Osiris had an evil brother named Seth.
Seth was jealous of Osiris. He wanted to be king.
One day, Seth tricked Osiris.
He made a beautiful chest and said: “The first person who fits in this chest will win!”
Seth measured the chest and made sure it was just right for Osiris.
Osiris got into the chest and closed the lid.
Seth locked the chest and threw it into the Nile River!
“Whoosh!”
The chest floated away on the water.
Isis searched everywhere for her husband.
Finally, she found the chest in a tree in Lebanon.
But Seth found it too. Seth cut the tree and threw the chest into the sea!
Isis cried and cried. She couldn’t find Osiris.
Osiris’s son Horus fought Seth and became the new king.
Osiris became the god of the underworld. He protected people after death.
Little friends, Osiris’s story is about love and justice. Even when people die, they can continue to help others.
What the Story Teaches Us # Osiris was a good king who was betrayed by his brother. This story teaches us to be kind and just, and to protect the people we love.
title: 057 Osiris and Isis

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a god named Horus.
He was the god of the sky and the son of Osiris.
Horus had a special eye called the Eye of Horus.
The Eye of Horus was very powerful. It could see everything.
One day, Horus fought with his uncle Seth.
Seth was a bad god who wanted to be king.
They fought a big battle.
Seth hurt Horus’s eye!
The eye was broken into pieces.
But the Eye of Horus was magical. It could heal itself.
The pieces came back together.
The eye was whole again.
The Egyptians believed the Eye of Horus could protect them.
They put the Eye of Horus on their tombs and temples.
They also used it in their writing.
The Eye of Horus became a symbol of protection and healing.
When people were sick, they would ask for the Eye of Horus’s help.
Little friends, the Eye of Horus was a powerful symbol. It taught people to be brave and protect themselves.
What the Story Teaches Us # The Eye of Horus was a symbol of protection and healing. This story teaches us to be brave and protect ourselves and others.
title: 058 The Eye of Horus

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a god named Anubis.
He had the head of a jackal.
Anubis was the god of the dead and the protector of souls.
When people died, their souls went to the underworld.
Anubis would check if the souls were good.
He had a special scale called the Scale of Truth.
On one side of the scale, he put the person’s heart.
On the other side, he put a feather.
The feather was from the goddess Maat, the goddess of truth.
If the heart was light, it meant the person was good.
“Whoosh!”
The scale went down on the feather side.
The person could go to the afterlife happily.
If the heart was heavy, it meant the person had done bad things.
“Boom!”
The scale tipped to the heart side.
The heart was eaten by a monster called Ammit.
The person could not go to the afterlife.
Anubis was fair. He always weighed hearts carefully.
Little friends, Anubis taught people to be good.
If you are good, your heart will be light.
What the Story Teaches Us # Anubis weighed hearts to see if people were good. This story teaches us to be good and honest, so our hearts will be light.
title: 059 Anubis Weighs the Heart

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a cat goddess named Bastet.
She had the body of a cat and the head of a lioness.
Bastet was the goddess of home, cats, and protection.
Egyptians loved cats very much.
They thought cats were special.
Cats could catch rats and snakes.
Rats and snakes could carry diseases.
So cats protected people from getting sick.
Bastet helped cats too.
When cats were sick, people would pray to Bastet.
“Please help my cat!” they would say.
Bastet would send her healing power to the cat.
The cat would get better.
Bastet also protected homes.
She watched over families and kept them safe.
Egyptians built temples for Bastet.
They put statues of cats in the temples.
Sometimes they even buried cats in special tombs.
Little friends, cats are special animals. Bastet was the cat goddess who protected them.
What the Story Teaches Us # Bastet was the cat goddess who protected cats and homes. This story teaches us to love and protect animals, especially cats.
title: 060 Bastet the Cat Goddess

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a god of wisdom named Thoth.
Thoth had the head of an ibis bird and long legs. He was very clever.
Before Thoth, people had no writing. They remembered things by drawing pictures on stone.
But drawings take a lot of space and are hard to remember.
Thoth wanted to create a better way to record information.
He watched the moon and noticed the phases change.
“Ah! I have an idea!” Thoth said.
He created hieroglyphics—a special kind of writing using pictures and symbols.
Thoth taught people how to write hieroglyphics.
Now people could write down stories, laws, and important information.
The Egyptians built pyramids and temples using hieroglyphics.
Thoth became the god of wisdom, writing, and knowledge.
Little friends, writing helps us remember important things and share knowledge with others!
What the Story Teaches Us # Thoth invented writing to help people remember and share information. This story teaches us that knowledge and education are precious gifts.
title: 061 Thoth and Writing

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a fierce goddess named Sekhmet.
She had the head of a lioness and the body of a woman.
Sekhmet was the goddess of war and healing.
She could fight enemies and heal sick people.
The pharaohs asked Sekhmet for help when they went to war.
They also asked her to heal their people when they were sick.
Sekhmet was very powerful, but she could also be dangerous.
Once, the sun god Ra sent Sekhmet to punish humans.
Humans had done bad things, so Ra wanted to destroy them.
Sekhmet became very angry. She attacked people like a lion.
“Roar! Scratch! Bite!”
Many people were hurt.
Ra felt sorry for them. He wanted to stop Sekhmet.
Ra had an idea. He ordered his servants to make 7,000 jars of beer and wine.
They poured the beer and wine into a river.
“Whoosh!”
The river became red and smelled like wine.
Sekhmet drank the red liquid.
“Yummy!” she said. “This is good!”
Sekhmet became drunk and fell asleep.
The people were saved!
From then on, Sekhmet was still the goddess of war, but she also protected people from disease.
Little friends, Sekhmet teaches us: even powerful things can be controlled with wisdom.
What the Story Teaches Us # Sekhmet was tamed by beer and wine. This story teaches us that even anger and power can be controlled with wisdom.
title: 062 Sekhmet the Lioness Goddess

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Egyptian mythology, there was a sacred river called the Nile.
The Nile was very important to the Egyptians.
It was long and wide. It flowed from south to north.
Every year, the Nile had a big flood.
“Whoosh!”
The river water overflowed and covered the land.
When the water went away, it left rich mud.
The Egyptians planted crops in the mud.
The crops grew very well.
The Nile gave the Egyptians food.
The Egyptians called the Nile “the gift of the Nile.”
There was a god of the Nile named Hapi.
Hapi had big, round breasts and a happy face.
He carried baskets of food.
Hapi brought the flood and the rich mud.
The Egyptians thanked Hapi every year.
They built temples for Hapi.
They gave offerings to Hapi.
Without the Nile, the Egyptians would have no food.
Little friends, the Nile was a special river that gave food to people.
What the Story Teaches Us # The Nile was a sacred river that provided food and life to the Egyptians. This story teaches us to be grateful for nature’s gifts.
title: 063 The Legend of the Nile

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a god named Brahma.
He was the creator god. He created the world.
Brahma sat on a lotus flower in the ocean.
From the lotus flower, a golden egg appeared.
The golden egg was called the Hiranyagarbha.
Brahma came out of the golden egg.
He looked around and saw the empty universe.
“Time to create the world!” Brahma said.
He thought and thought.
“Earth, sky, sun, moon, stars, plants, animals, people…”
Brahma created everything one by one.
He created the earth first.
Then he created the sky.
He created the sun and the moon.
He created the stars.
He created plants and trees.
He created animals.
Finally, he created humans.
“Live well, humans!” Brahma said. “Take care of each other.”
Brahma also created the four Vedas, the sacred books of India.
Brahma’s work was done.
The world was complete and beautiful.
Little friends, Brahma created the world with his thoughts.
This story teaches us to use our imagination and creativity.
What the Story Teaches Us # Brahma created the world from a golden egg. This story teaches us to use our imagination and creativity to create beautiful things.
title: 064 Brahma Creates the World

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a god named Shiva.
He was the god of destruction and rebirth.
Shiva had a special power: he could control water.
One day, a king named Bhagiratha wanted to bring the holy river Ganges down to earth.
The Ganges was in the sky. It was very powerful.
If it came down directly, it would flood the earth!
Shiva said: “I can help you.”
Shiva stood under the river.
“Whoosh!”
The Ganges water flowed into Shiva’s hair.
The water went down through Shiva’s hair and came out slowly.
It became a gentle river on earth.
The river was called the Ganges.
People used the Ganges water to bathe and pray.
They believed it could wash away their sins.
Bhagiratha’s ancestors were saved.
Shiva was a powerful but kind god.
He controlled the dangerous water to help people.
Little friends, Shiva taught people how to use water safely.
What the Story Teaches Us # Shiva controlled the powerful Ganges river to help people. This story teaches us to use our power wisely and help others.
title: 065 Shiva and the Ganges

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a god named Vishnu. He was the protector god.
Vishnu had a special power: he could take different forms to help people.
These special forms are called “avatars.”
Vishnu’s first avatar was a small fish. He saved a king from a big flood.
His second avatar was a giant turtle. He helped gods lift a mountain.
His third avatar was a wild boar. He dug up the earth from under the sea.
His fourth avatar was a man-lion. He fought a bad demon.
One day, a bad demon named Hiranyakashipu became very powerful.
He said: “No one can hurt me!”
But Vishnu took his fifth avatar—a small boy named Narasimha.
Narasimha had a human body but the head of a lion!
When Hiranyakashipu came home, Narasimha caught him—
“Roar!”
The lion god killed the bad demon.
Vishnu’s avatars always protected good people and fought bad things.
Little friends, Vishnu’s avatars teach us: when we face difficulties, we can be brave and strong!
What the Story Teaches Us # Vishnu’s avatars protected people and fought bad things. This story teaches us to be brave and help others when they need us.
title: 066 Vishnu's Avatars

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a monkey god named Hanuman.
He had the body of a monkey and the face of a human.
Hanuman was very strong. He could jump very high and run very fast.
One day, a princess named Sita was kidnapped by a bad demon named Ravana.
Sita’s husband, Prince Rama, wanted to save her.
Rama asked Hanuman: “Can you help me?”
Hanuman said: “Of course! I’ll help you rescue Sita!”
Hanuman jumped and jumped. He flew across the sky like a bird.
He reached Lanka, the demon’s kingdom.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
Hanuman saw Sita in a garden.
He gave her a ring from Rama to prove who he was.
Sita was happy to see Hanuman.
Then Hanuman fought the demon’s army.
“Roar! Whoosh! Bang!”
Hanuman was so strong that he defeated many demons.
He carried Sita back on his shoulder and flew home.
Rama and Sita were reunited!
Little friends, Hanuman was a brave and loyal helper. He taught us to be loyal to our friends and help them when they need us.
What the Story Teaches Us # Hanuman helped Rama rescue Sita. This story teaches us to be loyal and brave, and to help our friends when they are in trouble.
title: 067 Hanuman the Monkey God

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a god named Ganesha.
He had the head of an elephant and the body of a human.
Ganesha was the god of wisdom and success.
He could solve any problem.
One day, Parvati, Ganesha’s mother, asked him to guard the door.
“I’m going to take a bath,” Parvati said.
Ganesha stood by the door.
His father, Shiva, came home.
“Who is that?” Shiva asked.
Ganesha said: “My mother asked me to guard the door.”
Shiva was angry. He didn’t know Ganesha was his son.
Shiva fought with Ganesha.
“Bang! Whoosh! Scratch!”
Ganesha was strong, but Shiva was stronger.
Ganesha’s head was cut off!
Parvati came out of the bath and saw what happened.
She was very sad and angry.
“Who cut off my son’s head?” she cried.
Shiva said: “Don’t worry. I’ll fix it.”
Shiva looked around and saw an elephant.
“Perfect!” Shiva said.
He put the elephant’s head on Ganesha’s body.
Ganesha came back to life!
Ganesha became the elephant-headed god.
He was wise and powerful.
Little friends, Ganesha was a special god with an elephant head.
What the Story Teaches Us # Ganesha was created with an elephant’s head after an accident. This story teaches us that we can overcome problems and become stronger.
title: 068 Ganesha the Elephant God

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a prince named Rama.
He was a good and brave prince.
Rama married a beautiful princess named Sita.
They lived happily together.
But Rama’s brother, Ravana, was a bad demon.
Ravana wanted to marry Sita.
One day, Ravana kidnapped Sita!
Rama was very sad. He wanted to save his wife.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
Rama flew on his golden chariot.
He had an army of monkeys and bears.
They fought Ravana’s army.
“Bang! Whoosh! Scratch!”
Rama and his army were brave.
Finally, they found Sita.
Sita was safe!
Rama and Sita went home together.
They were reunited!
The people of Ayodhya were happy.
They celebrated Rama’s victory.
Rama became a good king.
He ruled the kingdom wisely and kindly.
Little friends, Rama and Sita were brave and kind.
This story teaches us to be brave and protect our loved ones.
What the Story Teaches Us # Rama rescued Sita from the bad demon Ravana. This story teaches us to be brave, loyal, and protect our loved ones.
title: 069 Rama and Sita

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a god named Krishna.
He had blue skin like the sky.
Krishna was a cowherd god. He herded cows in a beautiful village.
He was very playful and fun.
Krishna was also very strong.
One day, a big snake named Kalinga attacked the village.
“Whoosh!”
The snake was huge and scary.
Krishna stood up to protect the people.
“Don’t be afraid!” Krishna said.
He caught the snake.
“Bang!”
Krishna killed the snake and saved the village!
The people were safe.
Krishna was also very wise.
He taught people important lessons.
He said: “Be good, be kind, and help others.”
Krishna played the flute beautifully.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
The music made everyone happy.
People loved Krishna.
He was the most beloved god in India.
Little friends, Krishna was a playful and powerful god.
What the Story Teaches Us # Krishna protected people from a snake and taught them to be good. This story teaches us to be brave, kind, and helpful.
title: 070 Krishna the Blue God

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Indian mythology, there was a beautiful river goddess named Ganga.
She was the daughter of the sky god. She wore white clothes and rode on a crocodile.
Ganga lived in the sky, flowing as part of the Milky Way.
There was a king named Bhagiratha whose ancestors had done bad things. Their souls couldn’t rest.
Bhagiratha wanted to use Ganga’s water to wash away his ancestors’ sins.
He prayed for many, many years.
Finally, the gods agreed. Ganga would come down to help.
But Ganga’s water was too powerful! If she fell directly, she would flood the whole earth!
Shiva, the god of destruction and rebirth, stood up and caught Ganga with his hair.
“Whoosh!”
Ganga’s water flowed into Shiva’s hair and slowly came down to earth.
Ganga also came down with her.
She became a beautiful river flowing through India.
People use Ganga’s water to bathe and pray. They believe it can wash away bad things.
Bhagiratha’s ancestors were finally at peace.
Little friends, Ganga goddess teaches us: kindness and persistence can move mountains!
What the Story Teaches Us # Ganga descended to help Bhagiratha. This story teaches us that kindness and persistence can move mountains and help others.
title: 071 Goddess Ganga Descends

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Japanese mythology, there was a god named Izanagi and a goddess named Izanami.
They lived in a place called Takamagahara, the high plain of heaven.
The world below was dark and empty. There was no land, no sea, no sky.
Izanagi and Izanami wanted to create the world.
They stood on the floating bridge of heaven and looked down.
“Izanagi, take this jeweled spear and stir the ocean below!” Izanami said.
Izanagi took the jeweled spear and stirred the dark ocean.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
Water dripped from the spear.
The drops of water became an island called Onogoro.
Izanagi and Izanami climbed down to the island.
They stood on the island and married.
From their marriage, many gods were born:
The sea god, the wind god, the fire god, the mountain god…
They created all the islands of Japan.
Then they created the sun, the moon, and the stars.
Finally, they created humans.
The world was complete!
Little friends, Izanagi and Izanami created the world together. This story teaches us: working together with someone we love can create beautiful things.
What the Story Teaches Us # Izanagi and Izanami created the world together. This story teaches us that teamwork and love can create beautiful things.
title: 072 Izanagi and Izanami

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Japanese mythology, there was a beautiful sun goddess named Amaterasu.
She was the most important goddess in Japan.
Amaterasu lived in a beautiful palace in the sky called Takamagahara.
Every day, she went out of her palace and rode her chariot across the sky.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
Her chariot brought light and warmth to the world.
The plants grew, the animals played, and people were happy.
But one day, Amaterasu’s brother, the storm god Susanoo, was very naughty.
He broke Amaterasu’s palace and ruined her garden.
“Hey! You broke my things!” Amaterasu shouted.
Susanoo laughed and ran away.
Amaterasu was so angry that she hid in a cave.
“Whoosh!”
She closed the cave door and blocked it with a big rock.
Darkness covered the world. No sun, no light, no warmth.
Plants died, animals were scared, and people were sad.
The other gods were worried. They wanted to bring Amaterasu back.
They made a party outside the cave.
“Yay! Let’s dance! Let’s sing!”
They made a beautiful mirror and a shiny necklace.
The goddess Ame-no-Uzume danced and danced.
“Look! Look!” she shouted.
The gods laughed and clapped.
Amaterasu was curious. She peeked out of the cave.
The gods showed her the mirror. She saw her reflection!
“Wow!” Amaterasu said. “I’m beautiful!”
She came out of the cave, and the sun returned to the world!
Little friends, Amaterasu’s story teaches us: even when we’re sad, we can find happiness again. Friends can help us feel better.
What the Story Teaches Us # Amaterasu returned to the world after being tricked out of the cave. This story teaches us that friends and joy can help us overcome sadness.
title: 073 Amaterasu the Sun Goddess

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Japanese mythology, there was a storm god named Susanoo.
He was Amaterasu’s brother.
Susanoo was very naughty. He broke things and caused trouble.
Amaterasu was angry and sent him away.
Susanoo went to a village called Izumo.
A terrible monster lived there.
The monster had eight heads and eight tails!
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
The monster attacked the village.
It ate the crops and scared the people.
The villagers were afraid.
Susanoo said: “I’ll help you!”
He made a plan.
He told the villagers: “Prepare eight barrels of sake.”
The villagers made eight barrels of rice wine.
Susanoo put the wine in the fields.
The monster smelled the wine.
“Yummy!” the monster said.
It drank all eight barrels and fell asleep.
“Now!” Susanoo shouted.
He cut off all eight heads!
“Bang! Bang! Bang!”
The monster was dead!
The villagers were safe.
Susanoo was a hero!
Little friends, Susanoo was brave and smart.
He defeated a terrible monster with a clever plan.
What the Story Teaches Us # Susanoo defeated the eight-headed serpent with a clever plan. This story teaches us to be brave and use our brains to solve problems.
title: 074 Susanoo Slays the Eight-Headed Serpent

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Japan, an old couple found a big peach.
The peach was huge and red.
“Wow! This peach is beautiful!” the old woman said.
They took the peach home.
The old man cut the peach with his knife.
“Whoosh!”
A little boy came out of the peach!
“Hello!” the little boy said.
The old couple was surprised.
“We found you in a peach!” the old man said.
The little boy said: “I am Momotaro. I will protect you.”
Momotaro was strong and brave.
He decided to fight a bad demon who lived on an island.
He asked the old couple for help.
“Can you give me some food for the journey?” Momotaro asked.
The old couple gave him: millet cakes, sweet potatoes, and rice.
Momotaro took the food and went to the demon’s island.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
He flew on a bird.
On the way, he met a dog, a monkey, and a pheasant.
“Can you help me fight the demon?” Momotaro asked.
“Yes!” they said.
They fought the demon together.
“Bang! Whoosh! Scratch!”
They defeated the demon!
Momotaro and his friends went home safely.
Little friends, Momotaro was a brave hero who protected people.
What the Story Teaches Us # Momotaro was a brave hero who fought a demon with his friends. This story teaches us to be brave, kind, and work together with others.
title: 075 Momotaro the Peach Boy

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Japan, a bamboo cutter named Taketori-no-oku found a little girl in a bamboo stalk.
She was very small, like a fingerling fish. She grew up very fast!
“Taketori-no-oku, please take care of me,” the little girl said.
She ate only three grains of rice a day, but she was very healthy.
One day, the little girl said: “I’m not from this world. My real home is on the moon.”
She showed the bamboo cutter a shining object.
“Take this to the moon,” she said. “I’ll come back for it.”
The bamboo cutter took the object to the moon palace.
The moon goddess saw it and called Kaguya-hime back.
“Whoosh!”
Kaguya-hime floated up to the sky.
The bamboo cutter cried, but he knew she had to go back.
From then on, the bamboo cutter planted bamboo every day, hoping to see her again.
Little friends, Kaguya-hime is a beautiful story about a girl who had to return to her home in the sky.
What the Story Teaches Us # Kaguya-hime had to leave her human family to return to her true home. This story teaches us that sometimes we must say goodbye, but memories stay with us forever.
title: 076 Kaguya-hime the Bamboo Princess

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Japan, there was a strong boy named Kintaro.
He wore a red bib and held a small axe.
Kintaro was very strong. He could lift big stones.
He could wrestle with bears!
He played with animals in the forest.
A bear, a monkey, and a rabbit were his friends.
They played together every day.
“Hey! Let’s wrestle!” the bear would say.
“Okay!” Kintaro would say.
Kintaro always won!
One day, a famous warrior named Minamoto-no-Raikou passed through the forest.
He saw Kintaro wrestling with the animals.
“Wow! This boy is amazing!” Minamoto-no-Raikou said.
He asked Kintaro to join his army.
Kintaro agreed.
Kintaro became a brave warrior.
He fought many battles and protected people.
He was known as the “Golden Boy” because he was strong and brave.
Little friends, Kintaro was a strong and kind boy.
He taught us to be brave and protect others.
What the Story Teaches Us # Kintaro was a strong boy who became a brave warrior. This story teaches us to be strong, brave, and protect others.
title: 077 Kintaro the Golden Boy

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Native American mythology, there was a powerful bird called the Thunderbird.
The Thunderbird was huge! Its wings were as big as mountains.
When the Thunderbird flew, the wind blew hard.
“Whoosh! Whoosh!”
The birds under its wings turned into rain and lightning.
“Boom! Crack! Flash!”
The Thunderbird created thunder and lightning.
The Native Americans believed the Thunderbird controlled the weather.
They told stories about the Thunderbird:
“One day, a snake monster attacked the people. The Thunderbird saw it and flew down.”
“Whoosh! Bang!”
The Thunderbird fought the snake monster and won.
The people were safe again!
The Thunderbird also brought rain to the dry lands.
“Whoosh!”
Rain fell from the sky.
Plants grew, animals drank water, and people were happy.
The Native Americans respected the Thunderbird.
They built special totems with the Thunderbird on them.
The totems showed their respect and gratitude.
Little friends, the Thunderbird was a powerful protector. It taught people to respect nature and the power of the sky.
What the Story Teaches Us # The Thunderbird protected people and controlled the weather. This story teaches us to respect nature and the power of the natural world.
title: 078 The Legend of the Thunderbird

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Native American mythology, there was a clever animal named Coyote.
Coyote was a trickster. He was funny and mischievous.
At first, there was only water everywhere. No land, no sky, no plants.
Coyote wanted to create the world.
He found a giant turtle.
“Ah! I have an idea!” Coyote said.
He pushed the turtle into the water.
“Whoosh!”
The turtle became an island.
Coyote said: “I need more land.”
He found a basket of dirt.
He poured the dirt on the turtle’s back.
“Whoosh!”
The dirt spread out and became more land.
Coyote created mountains and rivers.
He created plants and animals.
He created people.
Coyote was happy with his work.
But Coyote was also mischievous.
He played tricks on people sometimes.
He made mistakes too.
But Coyote taught people how to live in the world.
Little friends, Coyote was clever and created the world.
This story teaches us to use our creativity to make the world better.
What the Story Teaches Us # Coyote created the world from a turtle. This story teaches us to use our creativity and skills to build a better world.
title: 079 Coyote Creates the World

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in African mythology, there was a trickster named Anansi.
He was a spider, but he was very smart.
Anansi wanted to get all the wisdom in the world.
He went to the sky god.
“I want all the wisdom!” Anansi said.
The sky god said: “You can have it, but you must carry it on your back.”
Anansi agreed.
He went home and put the wisdom in a basket.
“Whoosh!”
He tied the basket to his back.
But the basket was very heavy!
Anansi tried to walk, but he couldn’t.
He asked his son to help.
“Carry the basket for me!” Anansi said.
His son carried it easily.
Anansi was jealous.
He made a plan.
He said: “Let’s play a game of tag.”
Anansi ran away.
His son chased him.
Anansi jumped into a tree.
His son couldn’t reach him.
Anansi laughed: “Ha! Ha! I won!”
But the wisdom fell out of the basket!
Anansi was sad. He lost all the wisdom.
Little friends, Anansi was clever but greedy.
This story teaches us to be happy with what we have.
What the Story Teaches Us # Anansi tried to carry all the wisdom but couldn’t. This story teaches us to be content with what we have and not be greedy.
title: 080 Anansi the Spider God

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in African mythology, there was a debate between the sun and the moon.
The sun said: “I’m the most important! I give light to everyone!”
The moon said: “No, I’m more important! I light up the night!”
They argued back and forth, but couldn’t agree.
An old woman named Anansi the Spider heard them.
“Let me settle this,” Anansi said.
Anansi took a big pot and put it in the middle of the village.
“Whoever can fill this pot first wins!” Anansi said.
The sun tried to fill it with light, but the light was too weak.
The moon tried to fill it with moonlight, but it wasn’t strong enough.
Anansi filled the pot with water from a river.
“Water is more useful than light!” Anansi said.
The sun and the moon were both disappointed.
But Anansi said: “Actually, you both have important jobs. The sun gives light during the day, and the moon lights up the night.”
The sun and the moon realized they needed each other.
Little friends, the sun and the moon teach us: everyone has their own special job, and we all need each other!
What the Story Teaches Us # The sun and the moon learned they needed each other. This story teaches us that everyone has their own value and we should respect each other’s differences.
title: 081 The Sun and the Moon

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Polynesian mythology, there was a clever demigod named Maui.
He had magical powers. He could change his size and shape.
One day, Maui said: “I want to fish up islands from the ocean!”
His brothers laughed: “You can’t do that! Islands are too big!”
Maui didn’t listen. He made a fishing line from the fibers of a coconut tree.
He tied a hook to the line and a heavy stone to the hook.
He threw the fishing line into the deep ocean.
“Whoosh!”
The hook sank deep into the ocean.
Maui pulled the line carefully. “Pull… pull… pull…”
Suddenly, the line was heavy!
“Whoa! Something big is on the hook!” Maui shouted.
He pulled and pulled. The ocean started to shake.
“Boom! Boom!”
An island came up from the ocean!
Maui and his brothers were amazed!
They fished up more islands one by one.
They created many islands in the Pacific Ocean.
The people settled on these islands and built homes.
Maui also made the sun slower.
“Hey! You’re moving too fast!” Maui said to the sun.
He caught the sun and tied it down.
The sun asked: “Please let me go!”
Maui said: “Okay, but you must move slower.”
Since then, the sun has moved slowly across the sky.
Little friends, Maui was clever and creative. He taught us to use our imagination and skills to create new things.
What the Story Teaches Us # Maui fished up islands and made the sun slower. This story teaches us to be creative and use our skills to solve problems.
title: 082 Maui Fishes Up Islands

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Polynesian mythology, there was a girl named Moana.
She lived on a beautiful island in the Pacific Ocean.
Moana loved the ocean.
She loved to swim and sail.
Her people were islanders. They depended on the ocean for food.
But something was wrong.
The island was losing its trees. The fish were disappearing.
Moana’s grandmother said: “The fish are dying because the coral is dead.”
Moana wanted to save her island.
She found a magical canoe.
“Whoosh!”
The canoe flew across the ocean.
Moana sailed to a faraway island.
There, she found a demigod named Maui.
Maui had magical powers.
He could change his size and shape.
Maui said: “I can help you.”
Maui and Moana went on an adventure.
They fought monsters and solved problems.
Finally, they found the heart of Te Fiti, the goddess of creation.
“Whoosh!”
Moana put the heart back.
The island was saved!
The trees grew back. The fish returned.
Moana was a hero!
Little friends, Moana loved the ocean and saved her island.
This story teaches us to love nature and protect our home.
What the Story Teaches Us # Moana saved her island by returning the heart of Te Fiti. This story teaches us to love nature and protect our environment.
title: 083 Moana and the Ocean

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Celtic mythology, there was a hero named Finn.
He was a wise and brave warrior.
Finn had a special teacher named Finnegas.
Finnegas wanted to catch a magical fish called the Salmon of Wisdom.
“This fish knows everything!” Finnegas said.
Finnegas waited by the river every day.
He waited for months and months.
Finally, the Salmon of Wisdom appeared!
“Whoosh!”
Finnegas caught the fish.
He cooked the fish for his student, Finn.
“Here, eat this fish,” Finnegas said.
Finn ate the fish.
Suddenly, Finn started to understand everything!
He became very wise.
He could solve any problem.
Finn became a great hero and leader.
He protected his people.
Finn taught others what he learned.
Little friends, Finn ate the Salmon of Wisdom and became wise.
This story teaches us that knowledge is precious.
What the Story Teaches Us # Finn gained wisdom by eating the Salmon of Wisdom. This story teaches us that education and learning are valuable gifts.
title: 084 Finn and the Salmon of Wisdom

content:
The Story # A long, long time ago, in Celtic mythology, there was a magical creature called a leprechaun.
He was small, about the size of a child.
He wore a green coat and a green hat.
Leprechauns were shoemakers. They made beautiful shoes.
They lived in the forest.
