For thousands of years, Crescent Moon Spring has never dried up in the desert, called the “First Spring in the Desert.” Climb Mingsha Mountain, overlook Crescent Moon Spring, see desert and spring water depend on each other, marvel at nature’s wonder.
Best Experience: Ride camels up the mountain at dusk, watch the desert sunset. Watch the starry sky in the desert at night.
Zhangye Danxia: Seven-Color Danxia # Zhangye Danxia is one of China’s most beautiful Danxia landforms, called “God’s Spilled Palette.”
On red sandstone, colors of red, yellow, orange, green, white, gray-green, and gray-black appear, layered like a dream. Seven-Color Danxia Scenic Area has four viewing platforms—each angle is a painting.
Best Experience: Come at dusk, watch the sunset dye the Danxia golden-red, colors even more brilliant.
Jiayuguan: The First Majestic Pass Under Heaven # Jiayuguan is the westernmost pass of the Ming Great Wall, “The First Majestic Pass Under Heaven.”
The pass city was built between Qilian Mountain and Heishan Mountain, the throat of the Silk Road. Climb the city tower, see the vast Gobi, imagine the scene of camel caravans passing through, feel the desolation of “West of Yangguan, no old friends.”
Best Experience: Climb the city tower at dusk, watch the sunset dye the pass golden, feel the majesty of the frontier.
Special Experiences # Maijishan Grottoes # Maijishan Grottoes is one of China’s four great grottoes, famous for clay sculptures.
The grottoes were carved on cliffs, with plank paths hanging in the air—thrilling. Cave 4’s “Flower Scattering Tower” is Maijishan’s essence, with exquisite murals and vivid sculptures.
Labrang Monastery # Labrang Monastery is one of the six great monasteries of the Gelug school of Tibetan Buddhism, called the “World Tibetan Buddhist Academy.”
Red walls and golden roofs, prayer flags fluttering. Walk through the prayer wheel corridor, listen to monks chanting, feel the solemnity of Tibetan Buddhism.
Yellow River Stone Forest # Yellow River Stone Forest is a wonder by the Yellow River, with stone pillars standing in various shapes.
Take a sheepskin raft drifting on the Yellow River, take a donkey cart through the stone forest, experience the ruggedness of the Northwest.
Gansu Cuisine # Gansu cuisine is mainly noodles and lamb. Lanzhou Beef Noodles is Gansu’s calling card, “One clear, two white, three red, four green, five yellow”—clear soup, chewy noodles. Hand-Grabbed Lamb is tender and delicious, eaten dipped in salt and pepper. Niangpi is a type of liangpi, chewy and smooth.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Lanzhou is Gansu’s transportation hub, with airport and high-speed rail. Dunhuang and Zhangye both have airports and high-speed rail stations. Hexi Corridor attractions are scattered—recommend chartering a car or self-driving. Accommodation: In Dunhuang, stay near Mingsha Mountain; in Zhangye, stay near Danxia scenic area; in Lanzhou, stay in the city. Note: Mogao Grottoes require advance reservation—tickets are hard to get during peak season. The Northwest is dry—drink plenty of water, watch for sun protection. Gansu’s magnificence is hidden in those Silk Road relics.
The art treasury of Mogao Grottoes, the desert wonder of Mingsha Mountain, the colorful wonder of Zhangye Danxia, the majestic pass of Jiayuguan… each place is nature’s masterpiece.
Come to Gansu and retrace the Silk Road.
Tomorrow, we head to Qinghai to see the blue waves of Qinghai Lake and the sky mirror of Chaka Salt Lake.
title: Gansu: Silk Road Pearl Dunhuang Dream, Seven-Color Danxia Falls to Earth

content:
At eight in the morning, Guangzhou’s old city district.
The teahouse is buzzing with noise, grandpas and grandmas already filling the tables. Servers push carts through the aisles, stacked with steamer baskets—shrimp dumplings, siu mai, char siu bao, chicken feet… Grandma skillfully flips through the newspaper, Grandpa slowly sips Pu’er tea. One pot, two items, they can eat from morning until noon.
This is Guangdong’s morning tea, a lifestyle etched into the bones.
Guangdong is a place that makes you want to eat as soon as you arrive.
Province Profile # Location: Southern China coast, south of the Nanling Mountains Best Travel Season: October to following April (avoid humid hot summer) Highlights: Morning tea culture, Lingnan charm, food paradise, reform and opening up Must-Visit Attractions # Guangzhou: The Millennium Commercial Port’s Earthly Vitality # Guangzhou is a city with over 2,000 years of history, and one of China’s most inclusive cities.
Chen Clan Ancestral Hall is a gem of Lingnan architecture, three courtyards decorated with exquisite wood, stone, and brick carvings and pottery sculptures. Every detail shows the craftsmen’s dedication.
Shamian Island is a small island by the Pearl River, once the British and French concession. The island is filled with European old buildings and towering banyan trees—Guangzhou’s most romantic spot.
Canton Tower is the city’s new landmark, 600 meters tall, nicknamed “Slim Waist.” When lights come on at night, it’s Guangzhou’s most beautiful night scenery.
Best Experience: Morning tea in the morning, stroll Shamian in the afternoon, climb Canton Tower at night for the view.
Shenzhen: From Small Fishing Village to Innovation Hub # Shenzhen is China’s youngest first-tier city—40 years ago, it was just a small fishing village.
Window of the World brings together miniature versions of world-famous landmarks—“travel the world in a day.” OCT-LOFT is where artsy young people gather, with old factory buildings transformed into galleries, cafés, and design studios.
Dapeng Fortress is Shenzhen’s historical memory, a 600-year-old ancient city with blue bricks and black tiles, telling the story of this city’s past.
Best Experience: Visit Huaqiangbei electronics market to feel the vitality of “China’s Silicon Valley.”
Chaoshan: A Pilgrimage for Foodies # The Chaoshan region (Chaozhou, Shantou, Jieyang) is a paradise for food lovers.
Chaozhou Ancient City has a thousand years of history, with memorial archway streets lined with arcade-style old buildings, snack shops one after another. Beef balls, oyster omelets, guotiao strips, duck mother twist… everything makes you drool.
Guangji Bridge is one of China’s four great ancient bridges, with the middle section formed by 18 wooden boats connected as a floating bridge, dismantled and reassembled every morning and evening—the “world’s earliest opening and closing bridge.”
Best Experience: Stay in Chaozhou for a few days and try every snack in every alley.
Special Experiences # Shunde Flavor Seeking # Shunde is a “UNESCO Creative City of Gastronomy,” one of the birthplaces of Cantonese cuisine.
Shunde Fish Sashimi is a local specialty, fish slices thin as cicada wings, dipped in ginger-scallion-garlic oil, fresh, sweet, and smooth. Double Skin Milk is a Shunde dessert, rich milk flavor, melting in your mouth. Jun’an Steamed Pig, Lunjiao Cake, Daliang Stir-fried Milk… every dish is a classic.
Kaiping Diaolou # Kaiping Diaolou is a World Cultural Heritage, unique architecture blending Chinese and Western styles.
A century ago, overseas Chinese brought architectural styles they saw abroad back to their hometown, building one diaolou after another. Ancient Greek colonnades, Roman arches, Islamic domes… various styles mixed together, yet unexpectedly harmonious.
Danxia Mountain # Danxia Mountain is a World Natural Heritage, with red sandstone peak forests like burning flames. Elder Peak, Yangyuan Stone, Xianglong Lake—every spot is nature’s masterpiece.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Guangzhou and Shenzhen are transportation hubs with high-speed rail and flights to all parts of the country. Chaoshan also has a high-speed rail station. Accommodation: In Guangzhou, stay in the old city (Liwan, Yuexiu) to experience morning tea culture; in Shenzhen, stay in Futian or Nanshan. Note: Guangdong is humid and hot in summer—recommend visiting in autumn or winter. Go early for morning tea, or you’ll have to queue. Guangdong’s charm is hidden in that earthly vitality.
The leisurely chat of grandpas and grandmas in the teahouse, the bustle of night market food stalls, the beef aroma wafting from Chaoshan alleys… these daily moments are Guangdong’s most moving scenery.
Come to Guangdong and measure this land with your taste buds.
Tomorrow, we head to Guangxi to see the landscape of Guilin and the pastoral scenery of Yangshuo.
title: Guangdong: Sipping Morning Tea with One Pot Two Items, Lingnan's Earthly Vitality

content:
In the early morning, the Li River.
A bamboo raft slowly glides past, ripples spreading across the water. Green mountains on both banks reflect in the water, a fisherman wearing a bamboo hat, cormorants standing on the bamboo pole, waiting for the command to catch fish. Morning mist drifts among the mountains, distant peaks appearing and disappearing.
This is the scene on the back of the 20 yuan note.
Guangxi is a place that makes you want to stay.
Province Profile # Location: Southern China, bordering Vietnam Best Travel Season: April-October (Li River high water season) Highlights: Karst landscape, ethnic minority culture, border scenery, longevity hometown Must-Visit Attractions # Guilin Li River: Landscape Gallery # “Guilin’s landscape tops the world,” and the Li River is the essence of Guilin’s landscape.
From Guilin to Yangshuo, 83 kilometers of waterway, with fantastic peaks on both banks in various shapes. Nine Horses Painting Mountain has nine horses naturally formed on the cliff face—legend says those who can see nine horses are geniuses. Yellow Cloth Reflection is the most beautiful section of the Li River, the clear water surface like a mirror reflecting green mountains.
Best Experience: Take a bamboo raft from Yangdi to Xingping—this is the most beautiful section of the Li River. Arrive in Yangshuo at dusk to see West Street’s lights.
Yangshuo: A Small Town Amidst Landscape # Yangshuo is a backpacker’s paradise, and one of China’s earliest international tourist destinations.
West Street is Yangshuo’s soul, lined with bars, cafés, and craft shops. At night, tourists from all over the world drink and chat here, extremely lively.
Yulong River is a tributary of the Li River, quieter and more pristine. Take a bamboo raft drifting, with pastoral scenery on both banks—water buffalo grazing by the river, villagers working in the fields.
Ten-Mile Gallery is a cyclist’s favorite, riding along country roads with green mountains, fields, and villages on both sides—picturesque scenery.
Best Experience: Rent an e-bike and ride along country roads, stop at a farmhouse restaurant when tired, and eat a meal of beer fish.
Detian Waterfall: Transnational Grand Waterfall # Detian Waterfall is China’s largest transnational waterfall, connected to Vietnam’s Ban Gioc Waterfall.
The waterfall is over 100 meters wide, with a drop of over 70 meters, cascading in three tiers. During the rainy season, water volume is abundant and momentum is magnificent. Standing on the viewing platform, watching the waterfall cascade down, water mist permeating, rainbows appearing and disappearing.
Boundary Marker 53 beside the waterfall marks the China-Vietnam border—you can see Vietnamese villages up close.
Best Experience: Take a bamboo raft close to the waterfall and feel the cool water mist on your face.
Special Experiences # Longji Rice Terraces # Longji Rice Terraces are the masterpiece of Zhuang and Yao ethnic groups’ generations of cultivation.
Terraced fields spiral from foothills to mountaintops, like giant dragons coiled on the mountains. In spring when filled with water, the terraces are like mirrors reflecting blue sky and white clouds; in autumn when rice matures, it’s a sea of golden yellow—breathtakingly beautiful.
Ping’an Village and Jinkeng Red Yao Village are good viewing spots—you can stay in the villages to see sunrise and sunset.
Beihai Silver Beach # Beihai has “The First Beach Under Heaven,” with sand white and fine, water clear.
Weizhou Island is China’s youngest volcanic island, with volcanic rocks, coral reefs, and banana groves forming unique island scenery. Ride an e-bike around the island, watch sunset, eat seafood—this is the most pleasant summer experience.
Bama Longevity Village # Bama is a world-famous longevity village, with an extremely high proportion of centenarians.
The water, air, and magnetic field here are all considered beneficial to health. Many urbanites come to Bama to stay for a period, breathing fresh air and drinking longevity water as a health regimen.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Guilin has Liangjiang Airport, with high-speed rail connecting to all parts of the country. Yangshuo also has a high-speed rail station. Detian Waterfall is about 3 hours by car from Nanning. Accommodation: In Yangshuo, stay near West Street or by Yulong River; in Guilin, stay near Two Rivers and Four Lakes scenic area. Note: Bamboo rafts may stop running during the Li River’s low water season (winter). Detian Waterfall is most spectacular during the rainy season. Guangxi’s beauty is the kind that makes you want to stay.
Cycling through Yangshuo’s countryside, drifting on Yulong River, watching sunset at Longji Rice Terraces, spacing out on Beihai’s beach… time here seems to pass especially slowly.
Come to Guangxi and put your heart at ease.
Tomorrow, we head to Hainan to see the romance of Tianya Haijiao and the sunshine of Sanya.
title: Guangxi: Guilin's Landscape Tops the World, Yangshuo's Scenery Enters the Painting

content:
At dusk, Xijiang Thousand-Household Miao Village.
The sunset dyes the stilt houses golden, cooking smoke rising gently. Miao girls in full dress perform the Lusheng dance in the square. Night falls, lights of ten thousand homes come on, the entire village like a sea of stars. Standing on the viewing platform, watching this spectacular scene, marveling at the charm of Miao culture.
This is China’s largest Miao settlement village.
Guizhou is a place that amazes you.
Province Profile # Location: Southwest China, eastern part of Yunnan-Guizhou Plateau Best Travel Season: May-October Highlights: Hometown of waterfalls, ethnic customs, karst landforms, summer resort Must-Visit Attractions # Huangguoshu Waterfall: Asia’s Largest Waterfall # Huangguoshu Waterfall is Asia’s largest waterfall, 77.8 meters high, 101 meters wide.
Water cascades from a cliff, sound like thunder, water mist permeating. Water Curtain Cave is hidden behind the waterfall—you can feel the shock of the waterfall up close. Tianxingqiao is part of Huangguoshu scenic area, with water stone forests and Silver Chain Waterfall—another world.
Best Experience: Come to Huangguoshu in summer, when water volume is abundant and most spectacular. Walk through Water Curtain Cave, feel the shock of water cascading from above.
Xijiang Thousand-Household Miao Village: Living Fossil of Miao Culture # Xijiang Thousand-Household Miao Village is China’s largest Miao settlement village, with over 1,300 households.
Stilt houses are built against the mountain, layered and stacked—spectacular. Viewing Platform is the best place to see the village panorama—see morning mist at dawn, sunset at dusk, lights of ten thousand homes at night. Lusheng Ground is where Miao performances are held—you can watch Lusheng dance and Miao song and dance.
Best Experience: Stay in the village, eat a long-table banquet, drink “High Mountain Flowing Water” wine. Wake up early in the morning, see the village without tourists.
Libo Xiaoqikong: Emerald on Earth’s Belt # Libo Xiaoqikong is a World Natural Heritage, praised as the “Emerald on Earth’s Belt.”
Xiaoqikong Ancient Bridge is the scenic area’s symbol, built in the Qing Dynasty, a stone arch bridge spanning emerald green water. Water Forest is a unique landscape, with trees growing in water, roots intertwined. Wolong Tan is an emerald deep pool, with cascading waterfalls—beautiful beyond words.
Best Experience: Come to Xiaoqikong in summer, walk in the water, feel the coolness.
Fanjing Mountain: Maitreya’s Dojo, Sky City # Fanjing Mountain is a World Natural Heritage, a famous Buddhist mountain, Maitreya Bodhisattva’s dojo.
Red Clouds Golden Summit is Fanjing Mountain’s symbol, with two peaks connected by a bridge, like a sky city. Mushroom Stone is Fanjing Mountain’s wonder, a giant stone teetering yet standing for billions of years. Old Golden Summit is Fanjing Mountain’s highest point—you can see sunrise and sea of clouds.
Best Experience: Stay overnight on the mountain, watch sunrise and sea of clouds in the morning. If you’re lucky, you might see Buddha’s light.
Special Experiences # Zhaoxing Dong Village # Zhaoxing Dong Village is China’s largest Dong village, “First Dong Village.”
Drum Towers are the Dong village’s symbol, with five drum towers each unique. Wind and Rain Bridge spans the river, a masterpiece of Dong architecture. At night, you can listen to the Grand Song of the Dong People, feel the “Sounds of Heaven.”
Zhenyuan Ancient Town # Zhenyuan Ancient Town has over 2,000 years of history, “Oriental Venice.”
The Wuyang River flows through the town, with Ming and Qing buildings on both banks. Qinglong Cave ancient building complex is built against the mountain, hanging on cliffs—an architectural miracle.
Guizhou Cuisine # Guizhou cuisine is mainly sour and spicy. Sour Soup Fish is a Guizhou famous dish, with sour soup appetizing and fish tender. Changwang Noodles are a Guiyang snack, with blood curd, intestines, and noodles—numbing, spicy, and fragrant. Siwawa is a Guiyang specialty, thin pancakes wrapped with various vegetables, eaten dipped in sauce. Houttuynia is Guizhou people’s favorite—some love it, some hate it, must try.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Guiyang is Guizhou’s transportation hub, with airport and high-speed rail. Huangguoshu and Xijiang Miao Village both have direct buses. Accommodation: In Guiyang, stay in the city; in Xijiang Miao Village, stay within the scenic area; in Libo, stay near Xiaoqikong. Note: Guizhou has lots of rain—bring rain gear. Many mountain roads—prepare motion sickness medicine. In Miao and Dong villages, respect local customs. Guizhou’s beauty is hidden in those landscapes and villages.
The magnificence of Huangguoshu Waterfall, the charm of Xijiang Miao Village, the emerald waters of Xiaoqikong, the Buddha’s light of Fanjing Mountain… each place is nature’s gift.
Come to Guizhou and feel the charm of colorful ethnic customs.
Tomorrow, we head to Yunnan to see the wind, flowers, snow, and moon of Dali and the ancient town night scenery of Lijiang.
title: Guizhou: Landscape Gallery, Hometown of a Thousand Waterfalls, Colorful Ethnic Customs

content:
In the evening, Sanya Bay.
The sunset dyes the sky orange-red, coconut groves rustling in the evening breeze. Some walk by the seaside, some play ball on the beach, some sit in lounge chairs watching the sunset. In the distance, several fishing boats slowly return to port, lights beginning to flicker.
This is Hainan’s most common dusk.
Hainan is a place that makes you forget time.
Province Profile # Location: China’s southernmost tip, tropical island Best Travel Season: November to following April (avoid typhoon season) Highlights: Tropical scenery, vacation paradise, duty-free shopping, coconut breeze and sea rhythm Must-Visit Attractions # Sanya: Oriental Hawaii # Sanya is China’s most popular tropical vacation destination.
Yalong Bay is called “The First Bay Under Heaven,” a 7-kilometer crescent-shaped beach with white sand and clear water—Sanya’s most beautiful bay. Luxury resort hotels line the coast; staying here, you open the door to the sea.
Tianya Haijiao (Ends of the Earth) is Sanya’s most romantic spot, with two giant rocks carved with “Tianya” and “Haijiao.” Many couples come here to make vows and witness their love.
Nanshan Cultural Tourism Zone has a 108-meter-tall Guanyin statue on the sea—the world’s tallest Guanyin statue. Standing by the sea, watching the Guanyin statue towering on the water surface, solemn and sacred.
Best Experience: Stay one night at a resort hotel in Yalong Bay, and watch the sunset on a private beach.
Wuzhizhou Island: China’s Maldives # Wuzhizhou Island is Sanya’s most beautiful island, with crystal clear water, visibility up to 27 meters at its deepest.
The island is fully developed with various water activities—diving, jet skiing, parasailing, underwater walking… Diving into the seabed to see colorful coral and tropical fish is an unforgettable experience.
Best Experience: Take the first boat to the island in the morning to avoid crowds. Take photos on Lover’s Bridge, watch sunset from Sunrise Rock.
Haikou: The Slow Life of Coconut City # Haikou is Hainan’s provincial capital, more down-to-earth than Sanya.
Arcade Old Street is Haikou’s historical memory, with Nanyang-style arcade buildings, weathered walls telling century-old stories. Walking on the old street, seeing old teahouses, time-honored shops, old barbershops, feel this city’s earthly vitality.
Holiday Beach is Haikou’s most popular seaside bathing spot, with white sand and clear water, complete facilities. In the evening, locals like to come here to walk, barbecue, and watch the sunset.
Volcano Park is the remains of a volcano from thousands of years ago, where you can explore volcanic caves and learn about geology.
Best Experience: Eat a bowl of Hainan noodles on Arcade Old Street in the morning, watch the sunset at Holiday Beach in the evening.
Special Experiences # Boundary Island # Boundary Island is the dividing line between northern and southern climates of Hainan Island, also a beautiful island.
The water here is clearer than in Sanya, with fewer tourists. You can feed manta rays, watch dolphin performances, and go diving to explore.
Yanoda Rain Forest # Yanoda is China’s only tropical rainforest at 18 degrees north latitude.
Walking into the rainforest, towering trees block the sky, vines winding, streams babbling. Take a deep breath—the air is full of negative oxygen ions, a natural oxygen bar.
Duty-Free Shopping # Hainan is the world’s fourth offshore duty-free shopping zone.
Sanya International Duty-Free City and Haikou Duty-Free Shop gather world’s major brands. Cosmetics, watches, bags are much cheaper than on the mainland—a paradise for shopping lovers.
Special Cuisine # Hainan cuisine is light and fresh. Wenchang Chicken is first among Hainan’s four famous dishes, with crispy skin and tender meat, dipped in ginger-scallion-garlic oil—fresh and fragrant. Qingbu Liang is a Hainan dessert, with coconut milk, mung beans, red beans, job’s tears, and macaroni—cooling and refreshing. Coconut Chicken is a Sanya specialty, chicken boiled in coconut water—sweet and fresh.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Haikou and Sanya both have airports with numerous flights. The island has a round-island high-speed rail, making transportation convenient. Accommodation: In Sanya, stay at resort hotels in Yalong Bay or Haitang Bay; in Haikou, stay near Arcade Old Street. Note: Summer is hot and rainy—recommend visiting in autumn or winter. Choose legitimate operators for diving—watch for safety. Hainan’s beauty lies in its simplicity.
Sunshine, beach, coconut groves, ocean waves—without much embellishment, already moving enough.
Lying on a beach chair, drinking coconut water, watching clouds roll by, listening to waves hit the shore… time here seems to lose its meaning.
Come to Hainan and throw your worries into the sea.
Tomorrow, we begin our Central China journey, starting with Hubei to see the eternal romance of Yellow Crane Tower and the magnificence of the Three Gorges.
title: Hainan: At the Ends of the Earth, Amidst Coconut Breeze and Sea Rhythm

content:
In summer, Chengde Imperial Summer Resort.
The emperor’s temporary palace is hidden among green mountains and clear waters, with pavilions and towers, lakes and hills. A gentle breeze blows, bringing the fragrance of lotus flowers. Walking on the long corridor, watching swans leisurely swimming in the lake, imagining the scene of emperors escaping summer heat here.
This was the Qing emperors’ summer palace, and China’s largest existing royal garden.
Hebei is an underrated province.
Province Profile # Location: Northern China, surrounding Beijing and Tianjin Best Travel Season: May-October Highlights: Imperial gardens, seaside retreat, Taihang mountains and waters, Yan and Zhao culture Must-Visit Attractions # Chengde Imperial Summer Resort: The Emperor’s Back Garden # Chengde Imperial Summer Resort was the Qing emperors’ summer palace, built over 89 years, larger than the Forbidden City.
Palace Area is where the emperor handled government affairs, with the Hall of Simplicity and Sincerity built from precious nanmu wood, unpainted, simple and elegant. Lake Area imitates Jiangnan gardens, with Misty Rain Tower, Golden Mountain Pavilion, and Water Heart Pavilion—one scene at every step.
Plain Area is a miniature of Mongolian grasslands, with green grass where you can ride horses and practice archery. Mountain Area occupies three-quarters of the resort’s area—climb to the summit for a panoramic view of the entire resort and the Eight Outer Temples.
Best Experience: Come to Chengde to escape summer heat, stay overnight in the resort, and feel the emperor’s summer life.
Eight Outer Temples: Art Treasury of Tibetan Buddhism # The Eight Outer Temples are eight temples around the Imperial Summer Resort, blending Han, Tibetan, and Mongolian architectural styles.
Puning Temple has the world’s largest wooden Buddha statue—Thousand-Hand Thousand-Eye Guanyin, 27 meters high, carved from five types of wood: pine, cypress, elm, basswood, and fir. Putuo Zongcheng Temple was built imitating Lhasa’s Potala Palace, called the “Little Potala Palace.” Xumi Fushou Temple was built by Emperor Qianlong as the Sixth Panchen Lama’s temporary residence.
Best Experience: Visit the Eight Outer Temples in the morning, enter the Imperial Summer Resort in the afternoon—one day is just right.
Beidaihe: Summer Resort # Beidaihe is China’s most famous seaside summer resort, a royal bathing beach during the Qing Dynasty.
Dove Nest Park is the best place to watch sunrise—in the early morning, the sun rises from the sea level, ten thousand birds flying together, spectacular beyond words. Tiger Stone Park has giant reefs, a good place for photos. Biluota Bar Park is a good place for nightlife, with seaside barbecues, listening to the sound of waves.
Best Experience: Come to Beidaihe in summer, watch sunrise in the morning, swim during the day, eat seafood at night.
Shanhai Pass: The First Pass Under Heaven # Shanhai Pass is the eastern starting point of the Ming Great Wall, “The First Pass Under Heaven.”
Old Dragon’s Head is where the Great Wall enters the sea, with stone fortifications extending into the water like a giant dragon drinking. Meng Jiang Nü Temple tells the legend of Meng Jiang Nü weeping at the Great Wall. Jiaoshan Great Wall is the highest point of Shanhai Pass—climb to the top for a panoramic view of the pass and the sea.
Best Experience: Stand at Old Dragon’s Head, watch the Great Wall meet the sea, feel the magnificence of “The Great Wall of ten thousand miles spans the dragon’s head.”
Special Experiences # Baiyangdian # Baiyangdian is the largest freshwater lake on the North China Plain, the “Pearl of North China.”
In summer, ten thousand mu of lotus flowers bloom, pink and white flowers swaying among green leaves. Take a small boat through the reeds, watching water birds fly, listening to fishing songs.
Best Experience: Come to Baiyangdian in summer, view lotus flowers, eat river delicacies, stay in farmhouse courtyards.
Zhaozhou Bridge # Zhaozhou Bridge is the world’s oldest existing stone arch bridge, built in the Sui Dynasty, over 1,400 years ago.
The bridge is 64 meters long, without piers, with only one large arch—ingeniously designed. Ancients said it is “Wonderfully constructed and firmly protected, the best under heaven,” a miracle in architectural history.
Yesanpo # Yesanpo is a secret place deep in the Taihang Mountains, with canyons, waterfalls, and karst caves—beautiful scenery.
Hundred-Mile Gorge is Yesanpo’s essence, with deep canyons and babbling streams—a paradise for hiking enthusiasts. Juma River offers rafting—coolest in summer.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Shijiazhuang is Hebei’s transportation hub, with high-speed rail to all parts of the country. Chengde and Qinhuangdao both have high-speed rail stations. Accommodation: In Chengde, stay near the Imperial Summer Resort; in Beidaihe, stay in seaside guesthouses; in Yesanpo, stay in farmhouse courtyards. Note: Chengde is cool in summer, a summer resort. Beidaihe is crowded in summer—book accommodation in advance. Hebei’s beauty is hidden in those unassuming corners.
The imperial grandeur of the Imperial Summer Resort, the seaside charm of Beidaihe, the lotus scenery of Baiyangdian, the millennium wisdom of Zhaozhou Bridge… each place is worth your stop.
Come to Hebei and discover the underrated beauty.
Tomorrow, we head to Shanxi to see the Jin merchant legends of Pingyao Ancient City and the millennium Buddha statues of Yungang Grottoes.
title: Hebei: The Majesty of Yan and Zhao Lands, The Beauty of Taihang Mountains and Waters

content:
In winter, Snow Town.
Night falls, red lanterns light up, illuminating snow-covered small houses. Cooking smoke rises gently, the air filled with the scent of firewood. Walking on Xueyun Street, seeing those snow-covered houses, like mushroom houses in a fairy tale. Snowflakes fall, landing on shoulders, on eyelashes, in the heart.
This is China’s most beautiful snow scenery.
Heilongjiang is a place that makes dreams come true.
Province Profile # Location: Northernmost China, bordering Russia Best Travel Season: December-February (ice and snow), June-August (summer retreat) Highlights: Ice and snow fairy tale, China-Russia border, North Country scenery, Russian-style charm Must-Visit Attractions # Harbin: Oriental Moscow # Harbin is China’s most exotic city, “Oriental Moscow.”
Central Street is Harbin’s calling card, lined with European-style buildings, called an “Architecture Museum.” In winter, ice sculptures line both sides of the street—at night when lights come on, it’s magnificent. Buy a Madier popsicle, eat it on the street at minus 20 degrees—that’s Harbin people’s romance.
Saint Sophia Cathedral is Harbin’s landmark, a Byzantine-style building with a green dome, solemn and dignified. Ice and Snow World is the world’s largest ice and snow theme park, with ice sculptures, snow sculptures, and ice slides—a winter fairy tale world.
Sun Island is Harbin’s back garden—summer you can see squirrels and flowers, winter has the Snow Expo. Songhua River freezes in winter—you can skate, ride ice sleds, spin ice tops.
Best Experience: Come to Harbin in winter, wander Central Street, see Saint Sophia Cathedral, play at Ice and Snow World. Skate on the Songhua River, eat a Russian Western meal.
Snow Town: The Ceiling of China’s Snow Scenery # Snow Town is China’s most beautiful snow scenery, “China’s Snow Town.”
The snow here has high viscosity, falling on roofs, forming “snow mushrooms.” Red lanterns, wooden houses, white snow form a fairy tale-like picture. Xueyun Street is Snow Town’s main street, lined with various shops and guesthouses. Dream Home is Snow Town’s popular photo spot, with the most beautiful snow mushrooms.
Best Experience: Stay overnight in Snow Town, see the snow scenery without tourists in the early morning. At night, see red lanterns illuminating snow mushrooms, take a set of dreamlike photos.
Mohe: China’s Northernmost Point # Mohe is China’s northernmost city, “Arctic of China.”
Arctic Village is China’s northernmost village, where you can find the “Northernmost Post Office,” “Northernmost Sentry,” and “Northernmost Household.” In winter, you can see aurora here—the only place in China where aurora can be seen.
Best Experience: Come to Mohe in winter, see aurora, ride horse-drawn sleds, experience throwing boiling water that instantly freezes. Send a postcard from the “Northernmost Post Office,” stamped with “Arctic Village” postmark.
Heihe: China-Russia Border # Heihe faces Blagoveshchensk, Russia across the river, a China-Russia border city.
Standing by the river, you can clearly see the Russian city on the opposite bank. China-Russia Mutual Trade Zone sells Russian goods. Wudalianchi is a volcanic geopark, with volcanoes, mineral springs, and lava plateaus—a recuperation resort.
Special Experiences # Yabuli Skiing # Yabuli is China’s best ski resort, “China’s Ski Capital.”
Various levels of ski runs, from beginners to professionals can find suitable ones. Skiing, riding snow tubes, soaking in hot springs—the perfect combination for winter.
Zhalong Wetland # Zhalong Wetland is the world’s largest red-crowned crane breeding ground, “Crane Hometown.”
Come to Zhalong in summer, see red-crowned cranes flying and dancing in the wetland—elegant and beautiful.
Heilongjiang Cuisine # Heilongjiang cuisine is mainly Northeast dishes and Russian Western food. Guobaorou is a Harbin famous dish, crispy outside and tender inside, sweet and sour. Red Sausage is a Harbin specialty, Russian-style, eaten with da lie ba—perfect match. Demoli Stewed Fish is a Heilongjiang specialty, with tender fish and rich broth.
Russian Western Food is popular in Harbin—braised beef in pot, borscht, and cream mushroom soup are classics. Madier Popsicle is Harbin’s calling card, with rich milk flavor—most enjoyable eaten in winter.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Harbin is Heilongjiang’s transportation hub, with airport and high-speed rail. Mohe and Heihe both have airports. Accommodation: In Harbin, stay near Central Street; in Snow Town, stay in guesthouses within the scenic area; in Mohe, stay in Arctic Village. Note: Heilongjiang is extremely cold in winter—keep warm. Snow Town is crowded during peak season—book accommodation in advance. Seeing aurora requires luck—not every time you can see it. Heilongjiang’s charm lies in its ice and snow fairy tale.
Harbin’s ice and snow sculptures, Snow Town’s dreamlike snow scenery, Mohe’s aurora wonder… each place is a winter fairy tale.
Come to Heilongjiang and fulfill an ice and snow dream.
Tomorrow, we begin our Hong Kong-Macau-Taiwan journey, starting with Hong Kong to feel the charm of the Pearl of the Orient.
title: Heilongjiang: Ice and Snow Fairy Tale, North Country Scenery, Exotic Border Charm

content:
In the early morning, Longmen Grottoes.
The Yi River flows quietly, with Buddha statues densely carved on the cliffs on both banks. The largest Lushena Buddha is 17 meters tall, with a benevolent face, gazing down at all beings. Sunlight falls on the Buddha statues, golden light shining—solemn and sacred.
These Buddha statues have been watching over this place for 1,500 years.
Henan is a place that commands respect.
Province Profile # Location: Central China, middle and lower reaches of the Yellow River Best Travel Season: April-May, September-October Highlights: Source of Chinese civilization, ancient capital cluster, Shaolin Kung Fu, grotto art Must-Visit Attractions # Luoyang: Ancient Capital of Thirteen Dynasties # Luoyang is the Chinese city with the most dynasties as capital, known as the “Ancient Capital of Thirteen Dynasties.”
Longmen Grottoes is a World Cultural Heritage site, with 2,345 niches and over 100,000 statues—the peak of Chinese stone carving art. Lushena Buddha is Longmen’s symbol, said to be carved in the likeness of Wu Zetian’s appearance.
White Horse Temple is China’s first government-sponsored temple, “The Ancestral Court of Chinese Buddhism.” Ancient trees tower inside, incense smoke curling—a perfect place to understand Chinese Buddhist history.
Luoyang Peony is “National Beauty and Heavenly Fragrance.” Every April, Luoyang holds a Peony Festival, with peonies blooming throughout the city in brilliant colors. Wangcheng Park and China National Peony Garden are good places to view flowers.
Best Experience: Come to Luoyang in April to see peonies, visit Longmen Grottoes during the day, eat water banquet on Old City Cross Street at night.
Shaolin Temple: The First Famous Temple Under Heaven # Shaolin Temple is at the foot of Mount Song, the ancestral court of Chan Buddhism and the birthplace of Shaolin Kung Fu.
The Permanent Residence is Shaolin Temple’s core, with Mountain Gate, Heavenly King Hall, Great Buddha Hall, and Scripture Library progressing layer by layer. The footprints in the floor tiles of Thousand Buddha Hall are marks left by monks practicing martial arts.
Pagoda Forest is the cemetery of Shaolin Temple’s generations of eminent monks, with over 240 brick and stone pagodas—China’s largest pagoda forest. Each pagoda tells the story of an eminent monk.
Sanhuang Village is Mount Song’s most beautiful scenic area, with cliffside plank paths, Book Cliff, and suspension bridges—thrilling. Standing on the plank path, with bottomless abyss beneath your feet, your heart races.
Best Experience: Watch a Shaolin Kung Fu performance, learn a few self-defense moves. Climb Mount Song, watch the sunset.
Kaifeng: Dreaming Back to the Great Song # Kaifeng was the capital of the Northern Song Dynasty, depicted in “Along the River During the Qingming Festival.”
Millennium City Park is a theme park built based on “Along the River During the Qingming Festival,” recreating the prosperity of Northern Song Dongjing. Various folk performances in the park—fire breathing, stilt walking, cockfighting, Judge Bao judging cases—make you travel back to the Song Dynasty a thousand years ago.
Kaifeng Fu was the government office of the Northern Song, where Bao Zheng once judged cases. Daily performances of “Opening the Government Office” and “Judge Bao Judging Cases” are vivid and interesting.
Daxiangguo Temple was the largest temple in the Northern Song, where the story of Lu Zhishen pulling up a willow tree in “Water Margin” took place.
Best Experience: Go to Gulou Night Market in the evening, eat soup dumplings, fried jelly, and mutton pancakes—feel Kaifeng’s earthly vitality.
Special Experiences # Anyang Yinxu # Yinxu is the ruins of the late Shang Dynasty capital, a holy site of Chinese archaeology.
Simuwu Ding is the world’s largest bronze vessel, weighing 832 kilograms—a national treasure. Oracle Bone Script is China’s earliest mature writing, with over 150,000 oracle bones discovered at Yinxu.
Yuntai Mountain # Yuntai Mountain is a World Geopark, with canyons, waterfalls, and lakes—beautiful scenery.
Red Stone Gorge is Yuntai’s essence, with red sandstone canyons, babbling streams, and cascading waterfalls. Zhuyu Peak is Yuntai’s main peak—climb to the top for a panoramic view of the canyon.
Henan Cuisine # Henan cuisine is mainly noodles. Stewed Noodles is Henan’s representative, with rich broth and chewy noodles, served with mutton and cilantro—warm and satisfying. Hulatang is a Henan breakfast, spicy and fragrant, paired with youtiao—perfect match. Luoyang Water Banquet is a traditional Luoyang banquet, with 24 soupy dishes—unique flavor.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Zhengzhou is a transportation hub, with high-speed rail to all parts of the country. Luoyang and Kaifeng both have high-speed rail stations. Accommodation: In Luoyang, stay in the old city district; in Kaifeng, stay near Gulou; for Shaolin Temple, stay in Dengfeng city. Note: Luoyang Peony Festival is crowded—book accommodation in advance. Shaolin Temple scenic area is large—recommend a full day. Henan’s depth cannot be understood in a day.
Standing before the giant Buddha at Longmen Grottoes, feeling 1,500 years of vicissitudes; walking into Shaolin Temple, feeling the legend of Kung Fu; wandering Kaifeng night market, feeling the Song Dynasty’s earthly vitality.
Come to Henan and touch the roots of Chinese civilization.
Tomorrow, we begin our North China journey, starting with Beijing to see the magnificence of the Forbidden City and the Great Wall.
title: Henan: Five Thousand Years of Civilization in Central Plains, Half of Chinese History Here

content:
At dusk, Victoria Harbour.
The sunset dyes the skyline orange-red, lights in skyscrapers beginning to come on. On the Avenue of Stars, tourists look for celebrities’ handprints. At 8 PM, “A Symphony of Lights” begins—lights on buildings on both banks flash, accompanied by music, magnificent. Standing by the seaside in Tsim Sha Tsui, watching this brilliant scene, marveling at the Pearl of the Orient’s charm.
This is Hong Kong’s most classic scene.
Hong Kong is a city that makes you want to linger.
Province Profile # Location: Southern China, east side of the Pearl River Estuary Best Travel Season: October to following March Highlights: Shopping paradise, food capital, East meets West, international metropolis Must-Visit Attractions # Victoria Harbour: One of the World’s Three Great Natural Harbors # Victoria Harbour is Hong Kong’s soul, one of the world’s three great natural harbors.
Avenue of Stars has handprints of numerous celebrities—a must-visit spot for tourists. Star Ferry is Hong Kong’s oldest transportation—taking a boat across Victoria Harbour, seeing scenery on both banks, is Hong Kong people’s daily routine.
Best Experience: By the seaside in Tsim Sha Tsui at dusk, see sunset and night scenery. Take the Star Ferry, feel Hong Kong’s slow pace.
The Peak: Overlooking Hong Kong’s Panorama # The Peak is Hong Kong’s highest point, the best place to overlook Victoria Harbour’s panorama.
Peak Tram is the transportation up the mountain, with red trams running on steep tracks—very vintage. Sky Terrace 428 is the peak’s viewing platform, with 360-degree views of Hong Kong’s panorama. See skyscrapers during the day, see brilliant lights at night.
Best Experience: Go up the mountain at dusk, see sunset and night scenery. Take the tram down, feel the vintage atmosphere.
Disneyland: Fairy Tale World # Hong Kong Disneyland is China’s first Disneyland.
Cinderella Castle is the park’s symbol, Mystic Point, Adventureland, Fantasyland, and Tomorrowland each have their own character. At night there’s a fireworks show, with fireworks blooming over the castle—dreamlike.
Best Experience: Play all day, see the fireworks show. Stay overnight at a Disney hotel, feel the fairy tale world.
Ocean Park: Ocean and Amusement # Ocean Park is Hong Kong’s classic theme park.
Grand Aquarium allows you to see various marine life, Thrill Mountain has various exciting rides. Giant Panda Adventure has adorable giant pandas—a great place for family trips.
Special Experiences # Hong Kong-style Cuisine # Hong Kong is a food paradise, “Asia’s Food Capital.”
Tea Restaurants are Hong Kong people’s daily life—pineapple buns, milk tea, egg tarts, wonton noodles, each one classic. Tsui Wah Restaurant, Lan Fong Yuen, Australia Dairy Company are must-visit tea restaurants.
Dim Sum is the representative of Hong Kong-style morning tea—shrimp dumplings, siu mai, char siu bao, chicken feet. At Tim Ho Wan and One Dim Sum, you can eat authentic dim sum.
Roast Meats are Hong Kong specialties—roast goose, char siu, soy sauce chicken. Yung Kee Restaurant’s roast goose is Michelin-recommended.
Shopping Paradise # Hong Kong is a shopping paradise, a duty-free port, with goods cheaper than inland.
Harbour City is Asia’s largest shopping mall, Causeway Bay, Mong Kok, and Tsim Sha Tsui all have large malls. Ladies’ Market and Temple Street are open-air markets where you can find bargains.
Central and Lan Kwai Fong # Central is Hong Kong’s financial center, with skyscrapers—Hong Kong’s most prosperous place. Lan Kwai Fong is the gathering place for nightlife, with bars and restaurants lining the streets—extremely lively at night.
Tai O Fishing Village # Tai O is Hong Kong’s last fishing village, “Hong Kong’s Venice.”
Stilt houses are built on water, with fishing boats shuttling through. You can take a small boat tour, see Chinese white dolphins. Here preserves Hong Kong’s most primitive appearance.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Hong Kong has an international airport, high-speed rail directly to Shenzhen and Guangzhou. The city’s subway, buses, and trams are all convenient—recommend getting an Octopus card. Accommodation: Recommend staying in Tsim Sha Tsui or Causeway Bay, convenient transportation, convenient shopping. Note: Indoor air conditioning in Hong Kong is very cold—bring a jacket. Shop around when shopping, watch for authenticity. Hong Kong’s charm lies in its diversity.
On one side, skyscrapers’ modern metropolis; on the other, tea restaurants’ earthly vitality; on one side, Disneyland’s fairy tale world; on the other, Tai O’s fishing village charm.
Come to Hong Kong and feel the charm of East meeting West.
Tomorrow, we head to Macau to feel the glitz and glamour of the Oriental Las Vegas.
title: Hong Kong: Pearl of the Orient's Brilliant Night, East Meets West International City

content:
At dusk, Yellow Crane Tower.
The sunset dyes the Yangtze River golden, and the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge spans the river in the distance, trains rumbling across. Standing on the tower, watching the rolling Yangtze flow eastward, you think of Cui Hao’s poem: “The yellow crane has gone, never to return; white clouds float on for a thousand years.”
This is Wuhan’s most classic scene.
Hubei is a place with stories.
Province Profile # Location: Central China, middle reaches of the Yangtze River Best Travel Season: March-May, September-November Highlights: Chu culture, Three Gorges scenery, Wudang martial arts, City of Cherry Blossoms Must-Visit Attractions # Wuhan: The River City’s Jianghu Spirit # Wuhan is a city by the Yangtze River, composed of three towns: Wuchang, Hankou, and Hanyang.
Yellow Crane Tower is Wuhan’s landmark, “The First Tower Under Heaven.” Climbing the tower for a distant view, the Yangtze River, the bridge, and the city all come into sight. Inside the tower, poems from literati throughout the ages are displayed—each one telling the legend of this tower.
East Lake is China’s largest urban lake, six times the size of West Lake. In spring, cherry blossoms in the Cherry Blossom Garden bloom in clouds of pink and white. In the evening, walking by the lake, watching the sunset reflect in the water—extremely pleasant.
Hubu Alley is where Wuhan snacks gather—hot dry noodles, bean skin, soup dumplings, shao mai… eat your way through, satisfaction guaranteed.
Best Experience: Come to Wuhan University to see cherry blossoms in spring, eat hot dry noodles in Hubu Alley in the morning, walk by East Lake in the evening.
Three Gorges: Magnificent Landscape Gallery # The Yangtze River Three Gorges is one of the world’s most spectacular canyons, starting from Fengjie in Chongqing in the west, ending at Yichang in Hubei in the east.
Three Gorges Dam is the world’s largest water conservancy project, 185 meters high, magnificent in scale. Standing on the viewing platform, watching the dam span the river, water mist permeating during flood discharge, rainbows spanning across—spectacular.
Three Gorges Households is the most beautiful scenic area of the Three Gorges, nestled against mountains and by water, with stilt houses, ancient sailing boats, and fishermen’s lights forming a pristine landscape painting.
Shennong Stream is a tributary of the Yangtze River, with deep gorges and crystal clear water. Take a pea-pod boat drifting, seeing hanging coffins and plank roads on both banks, listening to boatmen sing Three Gorges boat songs.
Best Experience: Take a cruise from Chongqing to Yichang, spending three days slowly appreciating Three Gorges scenery.
Wudang Mountain: Immortal Mountain, Daoist Spirit # Wudang Mountain is a Daoist holy site, the birthplace of Tai Chi.
Golden Summit is Wudang Mountain’s highest point, with the Golden Hall standing on the peak. When clouds and mist swirl, it feels like a fairyland. At sunrise, the sea of clouds surges, golden light spreading in all directions—Wudang Mountain’s most beautiful moment.
Zixiao Palace is Wudang Mountain’s largest Daoist temple, with red walls and green tiles, magnificent in scale. Inside the hall, the True Warrior Emperor is enshrined, with flourishing incense.
South Rock Palace is built on a cliff, with “Dragon Head Incense” extending out from the cliff—a place where ancient pilgrims risked their lives to burn incense.
Best Experience: Stay overnight on the mountain, watch sunrise in the morning, learn a set of Tai Chi during the day.
Special Experiences # Shennongjia # Shennongjia is China’s only administrative district named “Forest Region,” covered in primeval forests, the “Ridge of Central China.”
Shennong Peak is 3,106 meters above sea level, the highest peak in Central China. Dajiu Lake is an alpine wetland, with nine lakes scattered on the grassland, cattle and sheep in herds, like an oil painting. Shennong Altar is a place to worship Emperor Shennong, with a giant Shennong statue standing in the mountains.
Enshi Grand Canyon # Enshi Grand Canyon is praised as the “Oriental Colorado.”
One Pillar of Incense is the canyon’s symbol, a stone pillar standing alone among peaks, 150 meters high, only 4 meters in diameter at its thinnest point, yet standing for a thousand years without falling. Yunlong Ground Fissure is a crack formed by crustal movement, bottomless, with waterfalls cascading.
Jingzhou Ancient City # Jingzhou is a famous city of the Three Kingdoms, where the story of Guan Yu carelessly losing Jingzhou took place.
The ancient city wall is well-preserved, 11 kilometers in circumference, and you can ride a bicycle around it. The Guan Yu Temple and Zhang Juzheng’s Former Residence inside the city tell the history of this city.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Wuhan is a transportation hub, with high-speed rail and flights to all parts of the country. Yichang has an airport, the starting point for Three Gorges tours. Accommodation: In Wuhan, stay near Jianghan Road or Yellow Crane Tower; on Wudang Mountain, stay on the mountain; for Three Gorges, take a cruise. Note: Wuhan is hot in summer—recommend visiting in spring or autumn. Shennongjia is at high altitude—keep warm. Hubei’s depth is hidden in those poems.
The eternal romance of Yellow Crane Tower, the magnificent grandeur of the Three Gorges, the ethereal spirit of Wudang Mountain… every scenic spot has endless stories.
Come to Hubei and understand the legends of the Jingchu land.
Tomorrow, we head to Hunan to see the fantastic peaks of Zhangjiajie and the night scenery of Phoenix Ancient Town.
title: Hubei: Playing Jade Flute in Yellow Crane Tower, Living with Green Mountains in Three Gorges

content:
In the early morning, Phoenix Ancient Town.
A light mist drifts on the Tuojiang River, stilt houses reflecting in the water. A Miao grandmother washes clothes by the river, the sound of wooden clubs echoing in the morning air. On Rainbow Bridge, early-rising tourists set up cameras, waiting for the first ray of sunlight to fall on the ancient town.
This is the border town in Shen Congwen’s writing.
Hunan is a place that captures your soul.
Province Profile # Location: Central China, south of Dongting Lake Best Travel Season: April-October Highlights: Fantastic peaks and rocks, Miao frontier charm, Hunan cuisine, red hot land Must-Visit Attractions # Zhangjiajie: Avatar’s Prototype # Zhangjiajie is China’s first national forest park, famous worldwide for the movie “Avatar.”
Yuanjiajie is Zhangjiajie’s essence, with over 3,000 stone peaks rising from the ground in various shapes. Hallelujah Mountain (formerly Southern Sky Column) is the prototype for the floating mountains in Avatar, standing alone among peaks, extraordinary in presence. Standing on Enchanting Stage, watching the sea of clouds surge, peaks appearing and disappearing like a fairyland.
Tianmen Mountain is called “The First Divine Mountain of Western Hunan,” with Tianmen Cave being the world’s highest natural mountain-spanning cave. Glass Skywalk is built on a cliff, with bottomless abyss beneath your feet—walking on it requires courage. Tianmen Mountain Cableway is 7,455 meters long, the world’s longest alpine passenger cableway.
Golden Whip Stream is Zhangjiajie’s most beautiful canyon, with crystal clear stream water and towering peak forests on both banks. Walking along the stream, watching monkeys jump in trees, listening to birds sing on branches—extremely pleasant.
Best Experience: Stay on the mountain, watch sunset and sunrise. Walk the glass skywalk and challenge your courage.
Phoenix Ancient Town: Shen Congwen’s Hometown # Phoenix Ancient Town is the most beautiful ancient town in Western Hunan, Shen Congwen’s hometown.
The Tuojiang River flows through the town, with stilt houses on both banks, and Rainbow Bridge spanning the river. During the day, wander on flagstone paths, seeing old streets, old houses, old city walls; at night, lights reflect in the river water, singing drifts from bars—extremely lively.
Shen Congwen’s Former Residence is a must-visit place to understand this literary giant’s life. Southern Great Wall is the Miao frontier wall built during the Ming and Qing dynasties, witnessing the history of Han and Miao peoples.
Best Experience: Stay in a stilt house inn by the Tuojiang River, see the ancient town without tourists in the early morning, space out by the river at night.
Changsha: The Fiery Star City # Changsha is a city with flavor, and a city with vitality.
Yuelu Academy is one of China’s four great academies, a millennium institution with unbroken scholarly tradition. Aiwan Pavilion is hidden in maple forests, where the verse “Stopping my carriage to sit and admire the late maple woods, the frost-touched leaves are redder than February flowers” was born.
Orange Isle is a small island in the Xiangjiang River, with a statue of young Mao Zedong standing on the island. On weekend nights, fireworks bloom—Changsha’s most beautiful night scenery.
Taiping Old Street and Pozi Street are where Changsha snacks gather—stinky tofu, sugar oil baba, spicy crayfish… eat your way through, spicy and satisfying.
Best Experience: Climb Yuelu Mountain in the morning, wander Taiping Old Street in the afternoon, watch fireworks at Orange Isle in the evening.
Special Experiences # Yueyang Tower # Yueyang Tower is one of the three great towers of Jiangnan, made famous by Fan Zhongyan’s “Note on Yueyang Tower.” “Worry before the world worries, enjoy after the world enjoys.” Standing on the tower, watching Dongting Lake’s vast expanse of misty waters, feel the sentiments of the ancients.
Nanyue Hengshan # Hengshan is one of the Five Sacred Mountains, “The Most Beautiful of the Five Sacred Mountains.” Zhurong Peak is the highest peak—climb to the top to see sunrise and sea of clouds. Nanyue Grand Temple on the mountain is the largest ancient architectural complex in Jiangnan, with flourishing incense.
Chenzhou Misty Little Dongjiang # Little Dongjiang is a paradise for photography enthusiasts. In the early morning, thin mist rises on the river surface, fishermen casting nets, fishing lights flickering—dreamlike.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Changsha is a transportation hub, with high-speed rail and flights to all parts of the country. Zhangjiajie has an airport, and Phoenix Ancient Town is about 1 hour by bus from Zhangjiajie. Accommodation: In Zhangjiajie, stay within the scenic area or in Wulingyuan; in Phoenix, stay in stilt houses by the Tuojiang River; in Changsha, stay near Wuyi Square. Note: Zhangjiajie scenic area is large—recommend 2-3 days. Phoenix Ancient Town is crowded at night—watch your belongings. Hunan’s passion is hidden in those chili peppers, and also in those landscapes.
Zhangjiajie’s fantastic peaks make you marvel, Phoenix’s night scenery makes you intoxicated, Changsha’s cuisine makes you satisfied. This Xiangchu land always has reasons to make you linger.
Come to Hunan and feel the collision of fiery passion and poetry.
Tomorrow, we head to Henan to see the millennium Buddha statues of Longmen Grottoes and the legend of Shaolin Kung Fu.
title: Hunan: Asking About Fantastic Peaks in Zhangjiajie, Listening to Tuojiang River in Phoenix Ancient Town

content:
In summer, Hulunbuir Grassland.
A green sea of grass stretches endlessly, under blue sky and white clouds, cattle and sheep in herds, horses galloping. In the distance, yurts are scattered like white pearls on the grassland. A breeze blows, grass waves rolling, floral fragrance wafting.
This is China’s most beautiful grassland.
Inner Mongolia is a place that opens your heart.
Province Profile # Location: Northern China, spanning Northeast, North China, and Northwest Best Travel Season: June-September (grasslands), September-October (poplar forests) Highlights: Grassland scenery, Mongolian culture, desert wonders, border scenery Must-Visit Attractions # Hulunbuir Grassland: China’s Most Beautiful Grassland # Hulunbuir Grassland is one of the world’s four great grasslands, covering 100,000 square kilometers.
Morigele River winds across the grassland like a silver ribbon. Ergun Wetland is Asia’s largest wetland, with forests turning colorful in autumn—breathtakingly beautiful. Birch Forest Scenic Area has dense birch groves, golden yellow in autumn.
Best Experience: Stay overnight in a yurt, watch the starry sky at night, see grassland sunrise in the morning. Ride horses across the grassland, feel the magnificence of “Vast sky and wild plains.”
Xiangshawan: The Singing Sand Desert # Xiangshawan is China’s largest desert tourism resort, named because the sand “sings.”
Sliding down from the dunes, the sand makes a “buzzing” sound, like an airplane passing by. Here you can ride camels, sand slide, drive off-road vehicles—experience the thrill of the desert.
Best Experience: Climb the dunes at dusk, watch the desert sunset. Stay overnight in a desert hotel, watch the starry sky.
Ejina Poplar Forest: Three Thousand Years of Watch # Ejina Poplar Forest is one of the world’s three great poplar forests, “Alive for a thousand years without dying, dead for a thousand years without falling, fallen for a thousand years without rotting.”
Every October, poplar leaves turn golden yellow, the entire forest like burning flames. Erdao Bridge, Sidao Bridge, and Qidao Bridge are the best viewing spots—each place breathtakingly beautiful.
Best Experience: Come to Ejina in mid-October, stay for a few days, watch sunrise and sunset, photograph the most beautiful poplar forests.
Manzhouli: Exotic Charm of a Border City # Manzhouli is China’s largest land port, bordering Russia.
Matryoshka Square has the world’s largest matryoshka doll, 30 meters high, colorful and brilliant. National Gate Scenic Area offers close-up views of the Russian town of Zabaykalsk. China-Russia Mutual Trade Zone sells Russian goods.
Best Experience: Wander Manzhouli streets at night, see the lights of Russian-style buildings, feel the exotic charm of this border city.
Special Experiences # Arxan # Arxan is a small city on the China-Mongolia border, with volcanoes, hot springs, forests, and lakes.
Heavenly Lake is a crater lake, with clear water reflecting blue sky and white clouds. Azalea Lake is beautiful when azaleas bloom in spring. Santan Gorge is a canyon formed by volcanic lava, with strange rocks standing.
Mongolian Culture # Come to Inner Mongolia, you must experience Mongolian culture.
Nadam Fair is the Mongolian traditional festival, with horse racing, wrestling, and archery—extremely lively. Yurts are traditional Mongolian dwellings—stay inside to feel the nomadic lifestyle. Hand-held Meat, Milk Tea, and Milk Tofu are Mongolian delicacies—must try.
Juyanhai # Juyanhai is a lake in the desert, the artistic conception of “Lonely smoke rises straight in the vast desert, the setting sun rounds the long river.”
In the early morning, thin mist drifts on the lake surface, swans and wild ducks playing in the water. At sunrise, golden sunlight spills on the lake—beautiful as a painting.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Hohhot is Inner Mongolia’s transportation hub, with airport and high-speed rail. Hulunbuir and Manzhouli both have airports. Inner Mongolia is vast—recommend self-driving or chartering cars. Accommodation: On grasslands, stay in yurts; in deserts, stay in Xiangshawan hotels; in Ejina, book in advance—rooms are hard to find during peak season. Note: Large temperature difference between day and night in Inner Mongolia—even in summer, bring a jacket. Many mosquitoes on grasslands—bring insect repellent. Ejina poplar forest is only beautiful in October—plan ahead. Inner Mongolia’s vastness opens your heart.
Galloping on horseback across grasslands, watching sunrise and sunset in deserts, feeling three thousand years of watch in poplar forests… this northern frontier land always has scenery that amazes you.
Come to Inner Mongolia and feel the vastness of heaven and earth.
Tomorrow, we begin our Northwest journey, starting with Shaanxi to see the shock of Terracotta Warriors and the ancient charm of Xi’an.
title: Inner Mongolia: Vast Sky and Wild Plains, Wind Blowing Grass to Reveal Cattle and Sheep

content:
In the early morning, a light mist drifts over the water in Zhouzhuang.
A black-awning boat slowly glides past, the boatwoman humming a soft Wu dialect tune, the sound of oars rippling across the water. White walls and black tiles reflect in the water, red lanterns swaying gently in the morning breeze.
This is the Jiangnan that countless people dream of.
Jiangsu is a place that makes you never want to leave.
Province Profile # Location: Eastern China coast, lower reaches of the Yangtze River Best Travel Season: March-May (spring flowers), September-November (clear autumn) Highlights: Water towns, classical gardens, Wu culture, hometown of scholars Must-Visit Attractions # Suzhou Gardens: Creating Worlds Within Small Spaces # “Jiangnan gardens are the best under heaven, and Suzhou gardens are the best in Jiangnan.”
Suzhou has over 60 existing classical gardens, with the Humble Administrator’s Garden, Lingering Garden, Master of Nets Garden, and Mountain Villa with Embracing Beauty listed as World Cultural Heritage sites.
The Humble Administrator’s Garden is the largest, centered around water with pavilions and towers scattered artfully. In summer when lotus flowers bloom, sitting in the Far Fragrance Hall watching the green leaves stretch to the horizon feels like being in a painting.
Lingering Garden is known for its architectural art, with one courtyard after another, each view changing as you walk. The famous “Three Peaks of Lingering Garden”—Cloud Capped Peak, Auspicious Cloud Peak, and Mountain Cloud Peak—are the finest examples of Taihu stones.
Best Experience: Enter the gardens when they first open in the morning, avoid the tour groups, and wander through the corridors alone, listening to your own footsteps echo.
Zhouzhuang: China’s No.1 Water Town # “Wu trees sway gently, Wu waters flow, Wu boats drift leisurely.”
Zhouzhuang has nearly a thousand years of history, still completely preserving 14 ancient bridges and over 800 original residents. The Twin Bridges, Shen Hall, and Zhang Hall—each place has its stories.
The most romantic experience is taking a black-awning boat, letting the boatwoman row you through stone bridges, watching people on both banks washing rice and vegetables by the river.
Best Experience: Stay overnight in a guesthouse in the ancient town, then go out at five in the morning to see Zhouzhuang without tourists.
Nanjing: The Weight of Six Dynasties # Nanjing is the capital of Jiangsu and an ancient capital with 2,500 years of city-building history.
Sun Yat-sen Mausoleum is built against the mountain, magnificent and imposing; the stone statues along the Sacred Way of Ming Xiaoling Mausoleum remain majestic after 600 years of wind and rain; by the Qinhuai River at Confucius Temple, painted boats glide through the night, reminding one of the verse “Mist veils the cold water, moonlight bathes the sand; I moor at night by Qinhuai, near the wine shops.”
Best Experience: Visit Ming Xiaoling in autumn when the ginkgo trees along the Sacred Way turn golden, walking on the path with fallen leaves crunching underfoot.
Special Experiences # Tea Tasting and Opera Listening # On Pingjiang Road or Shantang Street in Suzhou, find a teahouse, order a pot of Biluochun tea, and listen to a Suzhou pingtan performance. The soft Wu dialect melodies, accompanied by pipa and sanxian, can make a whole afternoon pass slowly and pleasantly.
Autumn Hairy Crabs # “When autumn winds rise, crabs’ legs itch.”
Yangcheng Lake hairy crabs are Jiangsu’s autumn seasonal delicacy. Full of roe and rich in paste, paired with a pot of yellow wine, this is the season Jiangnan people look forward to all year.
Yangzhou Morning Tea # “In the morning, skin wraps water; in the evening, water wraps skin.”
Yangzhou’s morning tea culture rivals Guangzhou’s. Fuchun Teahouse, Yechun Teahouse—a pot of tea with three-dice buns, jade shao mai, and thousand-layer oil cakes, eaten slowly until noon.
Travel Tips # Transportation: High-speed rail network is well-developed; Nanjing, Suzhou, and Wuxi all have high-speed rail stations. Travel between cities is very convenient. Accommodation: In Suzhou, stay near Pingjiang Road or Shantang Street; in water towns, stay at inns within the scenic area. Note: Gardens and water towns are crowded in summer—try to visit on weekdays or early mornings. Jiangsu’s slowness is an elegance etched into the bones.
Here, you can sit in a garden pavilion and space out all afternoon, listen to a boatwoman sing a tune on a black-awning boat, or listen to a pingtan master tell a story of scholars and beauties in a teahouse.
The dream of Jiangnan awakens in Jiangsu.
Tomorrow, we head to Zhejiang to see the misty rain of West Lake and the night scenery of Wuzhen.
title: Jiangsu: A Dream of Water Towns, Half the History of Jiangnan

content:
In March, Wuyuan.
Rapeseed flowers bloom across hills and valleys, golden seas of flowers extending from foothills to mountaintops. Huizhou-style white walls and black tiles dot the landscape, cooking smoke rising gently. A small stream flows past the village, reflecting blue sky, white clouds, yellow flowers, and pink walls.
This is the scene that countless photographers dream of.
Jiangxi is a place that makes you want to retreat from the world.
Province Profile # Location: Southeast China, south of the middle reaches of the Yangtze River Best Travel Season: March-April (Wuyuan rapeseed flowers), July-August (Lushan summer retreat) Highlights: Wuyuan flower seas, Lushan clouds and mist, millennium porcelain capital, red cradle Must-Visit Attractions # Wuyuan: China’s Most Beautiful Countryside # Wuyuan is praised as “China’s Most Beautiful Countryside”—see rapeseed flowers in spring, sun-drying crops in autumn, with different beauty throughout the year.
Jiangling is Wuyuan’s most spectacular rapeseed flower viewing spot, with terraced fields spiraling from foothills to mountaintops, golden seas of flowers stretching as far as the eye can see. Standing at the summit looking down, it’s like a giant oil painting.
Huangling is famous for “sun-drying in autumn.” In autumn, villagers dry red chili peppers, yellow corn, and white beans on rooftop drying racks—colorful, like a spilled palette.
Likeng is a small village with bridges and flowing water, clear streams running through the village, white-walled and black-tiled old houses on both banks. Sitting in a teahouse by the stream, watching elderly people wash vegetables by the river, ducks playing in the water.
Best Experience: Stay in a village homestay in spring, wake up at five in the morning to see the flower seas in the morning mist.
Lushan: True Face Unknown # “Viewed horizontally as ridges, vertically as peaks, from far or near, high or low, never the same. Not knowing Lushan’s true face, only because one is in the mountain.”
Lushan is famous for its clouds and mist, shrouded in fog over 200 days a year. Sea of clouds, cloud waterfalls, and Buddha’s light are all Lushan’s wonders.
Three-Step Waterfall is Lushan’s most spectacular waterfall, water cascading 155 meters down a cliff in three stages, magnificent in momentum. Locals say “Not visiting Three-Step Waterfall means you haven’t truly been to Lushan.”
Hanpokou is the best place to watch sunrise and sea of clouds. In the early morning, clouds surge beneath your feet, the sun rises from the lake surface, with ten thousand rays of golden light.
Guling Town is a small town on the mountain, called the “Exposition of World Architecture.” A century ago, Westerners built hundreds of villas here, still well-preserved today.
Best Experience: Come to Lushan for summer retreat, stay in an old villa, and wander through the clouds and mist.
Jingdezhen: Millennium Porcelain Capital # Jingdezhen has over 1,700 years of porcelain-making history, the “Porcelain Capital.”
Ancient Kiln Folk Customs Expo Area shows the complete process of traditional porcelain making—throwing, trimming, painting, glazing, firing. Master craftsmen use skills passed down through generations to transform a lump of clay into exquisite porcelain.
Taoxichuan is a creative park transformed from old factory buildings, with red brick buildings and towering chimneys now becoming art galleries, studios, and markets. On weekend nights, young ceramic artists set up their creations—dazzling array of works.
Best Experience: Try throwing clay yourself and create your own piece of porcelain.
Special Experiences # Nostalgia at Tengwang Pavilion # Tengwang Pavilion in Nanchang is famous for Wang Bo’s “Preface to Tengwang Pavilion.”
“Sunset glow and solitary ducks fly together; autumn waters and vast sky share one color.” Standing on the pavilion, looking down at the Gan River, imagine the magnificent scene of a thousand years ago.
Red Tourism Journey # Jiangxi is the cradle of revolution. Jinggangshan is the cradle of the Chinese revolution; Ruijin was the capital of the Chinese Soviet Republic. Take a red tourism journey and feel those eventful years.
Gannan Navel Oranges # Come to Jiangxi in autumn and taste Gannan navel oranges. Xinfeng and Anyuan oranges are most famous—thin skin, plenty of juice, bursting with sweetness.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Nanchang is Jiangxi’s transportation hub, with high-speed rail connecting to all parts of the country. Wuyuan has a high-speed rail station, and Jingdezhen also has an airport. Accommodation: In Wuyuan, stay in village homestays; in Lushan, stay in Guling Town; in Jingdezhen, stay near Taoxichuan. Note: Wuyuan is crowded in spring—recommend visiting on weekdays or staying in villages to avoid crowds. Lushan is a summer retreat—book accommodation in advance. Jiangxi’s beauty is hidden in those unassuming corners.
A small village in Wuyuan, a cloud in Lushan, a piece of porcelain in Jingdezhen… all are scenery worth savoring carefully.
Come to Jiangxi and rediscover your poetic self.
Tomorrow, we head to Shandong to see the majesty of Mount Tai and the hometown of Confucius.
title: Jiangxi: Sunset Glow and Solitary Ducks Fly Together, Autumn Waters and Vast Sky Share One Color

content:
In winter, Wusong Island.
In the early morning, thin mist drifts on the Songhua River. Willow trees on both banks are draped in silver, like jade trees, crystal clear. Sunlight penetrates the thin mist, shining on the rime, sparkling. Walking on the island, you feel like you’re in a fairy tale world.
This is one of China’s four natural wonders.
Jilin is a place that amazes you.
Province Profile # Location: Central Northeast China, by the Songhua River Best Travel Season: December-February (rime), July-August (Changbai Mountain) Highlights: Changbai Heavenly Lake, rime wonder, Korean ethnic culture, film city Must-Visit Attractions # Changbai Mountain: Northeast’s First Sacred Mountain # Changbai Mountain is Northeast China’s highest peak, “Roof of Northeast,” the birthplace of the Manchu people.
Heavenly Lake is Changbai Mountain’s soul, China’s largest volcanic crater lake, 2,189 meters above sea level. The lake water is azure blue, reflecting the surrounding 16 peaks. Standing on the viewing platform, overlooking Heavenly Lake, marveling at nature’s wonder.
Changbai Waterfall flows from Heavenly Lake, with a 68-meter drop—magnificent in momentum. Underground Forest is a wonder formed after volcanic eruption, with primeval forest hidden in the crater. Green Deep Pool is Changbai Mountain’s most beautiful small waterfall, with emerald pool water and cascading waterfall—picturesque.
Best Experience: Come to Changbai Mountain in summer, see Heavenly Lake, see waterfalls, see flower seas. Come to Changbai Mountain in winter, ski, soak in hot springs, see snow scenery.
Wusong Island: Jade Trees and Silver Flowers # Wusong Island is China’s best place to view rime, one of “China’s Four Natural Wonders.”
Every December to the following February, water vapor from the Songhua River condenses in the cold air, forming rime. Willow trees on both banks are draped in silver, like jade trees, crystal clear.
Best Experience: Come to Wusong Island in the early morning, see rime at sunrise. When the sun rises, rime sparkles in the sunlight—breathtakingly beautiful.
Yanbian: Korean Ethnic Culture # Yanbian is China’s largest Korean ethnic settlement, with rich Korean ethnic culture.
Yanji is Yanbian’s capital, a paradise of Korean ethnic cuisine. Cold noodles, stone pot bibimbap, roast meat, rice cakes… everything makes you drool. Chinese Korean Ethnic Culture Park allows you to experience Korean ethnic culture, wear hanbok, perform farmer’s dance.
Fangchuan is where China, North Korea, and Russia meet, “One glance at three countries.” Standing on Longhu Pavilion, you can see North Korea across the Tumen River and Russia in the distance.
Best Experience: Eat authentic Korean ethnic cuisine in Yanji, wear hanbok for photos.
Changchun: Film City # Changchun is the cradle of New China’s film industry, “Film City.”
Changying Century City is China’s first world-class film theme park, where you can experience various film special effects. Changchun Film Studio is New China’s first film studio, where you can understand Chinese film history.
Puppet Emperor’s Palace Museum is Pu Yi’s “imperial palace,” understanding the history of the puppet Manchukuo. Jingyuetan is Changchun’s back garden, with forests, lakes, and ski slopes—a great place for leisure.
Special Experiences # Chagan Lake Winter Fishing # Chagan Lake Winter Fishing is the last fishing and hunting culture in northern China, “Fish Leaping from Ice Lake.”
Every winter, fishermen chisel holes, set nets, and pull nets on the ice—one net can catch hundreds of thousands of jin of fish. The scene is spectacular, a paradise for photography enthusiasts.
Goguryeo Sites # Ji’an Goguryeo Sites are a World Cultural Heritage, ruins of the Goguryeo Kingdom.
General’s Tomb is a Goguryeo king’s mausoleum, “Oriental Pyramid.” Haotai King Stele records Goguryeo’s history—precious material for studying Goguryeo.
Jilin Cuisine # Jilin cuisine is mainly Northeast dishes and Korean ethnic cuisine. Cold Noodles are a Korean ethnic specialty, with chewy noodles and sweet-sour soup—most refreshing in summer. Stone Pot Bibimbap is a Korean ethnic classic, with rice and various vegetables and chili sauce—spicy and delicious. Guobaorou and Little Chicken Stewed with Mushrooms are Northeast classics, large portions and affordable.
Jilin Ginseng, Antler, and Mink Fur are the “Three Treasures of Northeast”—good souvenirs.
Travel Tips # Transportation: Changchun is Jilin’s transportation hub, with airport and high-speed rail. Yanji and Changbai Mountain both have airports. Accommodation: At Changbai Mountain, stay in Erdaobaihe Town; on Wusong Island, stay in farmhouses on the island; in Yanji, stay in the city. Note: Changbai Mountain is at high altitude—keep warm. Wake up early to see rime—best time is early morning. Northeast is cold in winter—keep warm. Jilin’s beauty is hidden in those natural wonders.
The Heavenly Lake fairyland of Changbai Mountain, the jade trees and silver flowers of Wusong Island, the Korean ethnic culture of Yanbian… each place is nature’s gift.
Come to Jilin and feel the magnificence of the Northeast.
Tomorrow, we head to Heilongjiang to see the winter fairy tale of Ice and Snow World and the dreamlike scenery of Snow Town.
title: Jilin: Heavenly Lake's Beauty Under Changbai Mountain, Jade Trees and Silver Flowers on Wusong Island

content:
In summer, Dalian Xinghai Square.
The sea breeze carries the scent of salt, seagulls circling overhead. Some sunbathe on the beach, some play in the water, some cycle on the wooden boardwalk. In the distance, the cross-sea bridge spans the bay—magnificent and beautiful.
This is Northeast China’s most romantic seaside city.
Liaoning is a place with stories.
Province Profile # Location: Southern Northeast China, between Bohai Sea and Yellow Sea Best Travel Season: May-October Highlights: Qing Dynasty birthplace, seaside scenery, industrial heritage, Northeast cuisine Must-Visit Attractions # Shenyang Imperial Palace: Capital of Two Generations of Emperors # Shenyang Imperial Palace is one of China’s two existing palace architectural complexes, the imperial palace before the Qing Dynasty entered the pass.
Dazheng Hall was built by Nurhaci, an octagonal building blending Manchu, Mongolian, and Han styles. Chongzheng Hall was Huang Taiji’s office, solemn and dignified. Wensu Pavilion houses the “Complete Library of the Four Treasuries,” a royal library.
Compared to Beijing’s Forbidden City, Shenyang Imperial Palace is smaller but has more Manchu character. Walking through the palace, imagining Nurhaci and Huang Taiji strategizing here, feel the history of the Qing Dynasty’s rise.
Best Experience: Hire a guide to hear stories of the Qing Dynasty’s rise. Come to Shenyang Imperial Palace in winter, see the palace in snow—unique charm.
Dalian: Romantic City of the North # Dalian is one of China’s most romantic seaside cities, “Pearl of the North.”
Xinghai Square is Asia’s largest city square—you can see the sea, feed seagulls, fly kites. Binhai Road is Dalian’s most beautiful road, with mountains on one side and sea on the other—picturesque scenery along the way. Tiger Beach Ocean Park allows you to see polar animals and marine life—a great place for family trips.
Golden Pebble Beach has unique marine erosion landforms, “Dinosaur Exploring the Sea” and “Great Peng Spreading Wings”—lifelike. Discovery Kingdom is a large theme park, suitable for young people and families.
Best Experience: Come to Dalian in summer to escape heat, cycle on Binhai Road, watch sunset at Xinghai Square.
Panjin Red Beach: Nature’s Palette # Panjin Red Beach is the world’s largest reed wetland. Every autumn, seablite grass turns red, forming a red ocean.
Red beach, golden reeds, blue sky, white migratory birds form a colorful picture. Boardwalk is the best route to view Red Beach—you can take a boat through the reeds.
Best Experience: Come to Panjin in September-October, see Red Beach at its most spectacular moment.
Benxi Water Cave: Underground Wonder # Benxi Water Cave is the world’s largest water-filled karst cave, “Treasure of the North.”
Inside the cave, stalactites are in various shapes, with an underground river winding through. Take a boat through the cave, seeing all kinds of strangely shaped stalactites, marveling at nature’s uncanny workmanship.
Special Experiences # Zhang Xueliang’s Former Residence # Zhang Xueliang’s Former Residence is the official residence of Zhang Zuolin and Zhang Xueliang father and son, “Commander’s Mansion.”
